Why a US-Russia showdown left Morocco celebrating
- Published
Morocco has welcomed the end of a decades-long UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after a diplomatic showdown between the US and Russia left the Security Council unable to agree on its future.
The council failed on Friday to renew the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (Minurso) after Russia vetoed a US-backed proposal. A rival Russian draft to extend the mission also failed to secure enough votes.
The decision raises questions about the future of Africa's longest territorial dispute and the fragile ceasefire between Morocco, which claims Western Sahara, and the Polisario Front which has been fighting for the territory's independence for more than 50 years.
Here is what you need to know.
Why is Western Sahara disputed?
Western Sahara, on Africa's north-west coast, was a Spanish colony until 1975. It has significant phosphate reserves and valuable fishing grounds along its Atlantic coast.
As Spain prepared to withdraw, both Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory.
The International Court of Justice found historical ties of allegiance but no territorial sovereignty that overrode the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination.
Morocco's then King Hassan II responded by organising the Green March. On 6 November 1975 about 350,000 Moroccan civilians entered the territory in a mass demonstration intended to put pressure on Spain.
Days later, Spain signed the Madrid Accords with Morocco and Mauritania, agreeing to transfer administrative control. Morocco took the northern two-thirds and Mauritania the southern third. The agreement did not settle the question of sovereignty.
The Polisario Front, an independence movement founded in 1973, opposed the deal. It saw it as replacing Spanish colonial rule with Moroccan and Mauritanian control.
Mauritania renounced its claim in 1979, but Morocco continued fighting Polisario.
Algeria became Polisario's main regional ally, providing military support and hosting its leadership and thousands of Sahrawi refugees in camps near the city of Tindouf.
The North African country says its position is based on the right to self-determination, while Morocco sees Western Sahara as an integral part of its territory.
Morocco and Algeria fought a brief border war in 1963 over disagreements about territory inherited from French colonial rule. Their relationship has remained tense, with Western Sahara at the centre of their dispute.
What was the UN's mission role?
After 16 years of fighting, Morocco and Polisario agreed to a UN-brokered ceasefire in 1991, with the territory divided by a sand wall, or berm, to keep the rival forces apart.
The UN established Minurso to monitor the ceasefire and organise a referendum on the territory's future. Sahrawis were meant to choose between independence and integration with Morocco.
The vote was scheduled for 1992 but never took place. The two sides could not agree on who would be eligible to participate, with disputes over voter identification becoming a major obstacle.
In 2007, Morocco put forward a proposal for autonomy, which would see Sahrawis managing their internal affairs, while Rabat retained control over defence and foreign relations.
The Polisario Front and Algeria rejected the plan, insisting on a referendum that included independence as an option.
Years of UN-sponsored negotiations failed to produce a breakthrough.
The ceasefire broke down in November 2020, when Polisario said it was resuming armed struggle.
But following a long diplomatic campaign by Morocco, the UN Security Council voted in 2025 in favour of a resolution backing the autonomy plan as the "most feasible" solution for the disputed territory.
While most Sahrawis live in the part of Western Sahara controlled by Morocco, tens of thousands are estimated to be in refugee camps in Algeria.
What happened at the UN?
The US proposed extending Minurso's mandate for another year, but its draft went beyond the usual renewal.
It would have removed the word "referendum" from the mission's name and made Morocco's autonomy proposal the sole basis for further negotiations.
The draft received the support of 11 of the Security Council's 15 members, including France and the UK but Russia vetoed it, arguing that it was too favourable to Morocco.
Russia then proposed extending Minurso's mandate without changing its terms. That draft also failed, receiving only two votes in favour.
Minurso's mandate expired at the end of Saturday, 31 October. The UN said the following day that the mission had entered a liquidation period, with a reduced team overseeing the transfer of military equipment and other assets.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination must be respected and warned of the risk of renewed hostilities.
The Polisario Front condemned the US proposal. Its representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing it, saying it would "torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process" and threaten regional and international peace.
Morocco, meanwhile, said the mission's personnel and equipment should leave the territory in the coming days, arguing that Western Sahara issue should no longer be considered by the Security Council.
Minurso had 155 military personnel and was expected to cost $62m (£46m) in the financial year beginning in June, according to a UN report.
Why is Morocco celebrating the end of the UN mission?
Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew Minurso's mandate.
In Laayoune, the territory's largest city, footage showed people celebrating, waving Moroccan flags and displaying portraits of King Mohammed VI.
"The decision is an opportunity for Rabat to challenge what it sees as an international mechanism that has failed to resolve the dispute," Issam Laaroussi, a Moroccan expert in international relations, tells the BBC.
He said Morocco would now have more room to push its autonomy proposal and shift negotiations away from a referendum on independence towards autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty.
The decision does not, however, change Western Sahara's legal status or amount to international recognition of Moroccan sovereignty.
Western Sahara remains on the UN list of non-self-governing territories, while the African Union officially recognises its independence, as the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR).
But the decision comes after several countries backed the position of Morocco, which in recent years has made securing international support for its claim a central part of its foreign policy.
In 2020, the US recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara as part of an agreement to establish diplomatic relations between Morocco and Israel.
France also backed Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for resolving the dispute in 2024.
Morocco rejoined the African Union in 2017, more than three decades after leaving its predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in protest at the SADR's admission.
Since returning, Rabat has sought to build support for its position from within the organisation. At least 10 African countries have opened diplomatic missions in the territory in support of Rabat.
"Morocco is not necessarily seeking to abandon the UN process, but to change the framework for negotiations and draw greater support from regional organisations," says Laaroussi.
Addressing a special joint session of parliament on Monday, House of Representatives Speaker Ahmed Touizi hailed the end of Minurso as a victory for the country's diplomacy.
He said the country should now move from "managing the dispute to implementing its autonomy plan under Moroccan sovereignty, while pressing ahead with development projects in the territory."
Could this lead to a renewed war?
The fear is that Minurso's departure could lead to renewed fighting.
The mission has monitored military developments and helped reduce the risk of escalation.
Aid organisation Oxfam warned that losing its monitoring and de-escalation role could undermine stability, with serious consequences for civilians.
Laaroussi admits that the mission's departure could create security gaps.
"Minurso's departure does not create the original conflict, because the conflict is already there, but it could aggravate an already fragile security environment," he says.
The UN decision has also fuelled nationalist rhetoric online.
Several Moroccan users have shared AI-generated images of themselves in military uniform, declaring their readiness to fight for Morocco's sovereignty over Western Sahara.
In Morocco, Western Sahara is widely regarded as a national cause. Political parties that are often divided on other issues are united in supporting the country's claim to sovereignty over the territory.
Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita has said the end of the mission does not mean the end of the ceasefire, and that Rabat remains committed to it "within respect of its security and sovereignty."
Polisario has not said what it will do next.
Any resumption of fighting could well draw in Algeria, as tensions with Morocco remain high.
According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), both countries significantly increased military spending last year, with SIPRI citing their dispute over Western Sahara as a key driver.
Algeria spent an estimated $25.4bn, more than four time Morocco's $6.3bn.

Three security personnel injured in attack by terrorists in Kulgam
NEW DELHI: Terrorists riding a motorcycle opened fire on Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel deployed at a checkpoint in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on Wednesday afternoon, injuring three security personnel. A search operation has been launched to track down the attackers. A CRPF official said that two of the three injured personnel were stable, while the third was in critical condition.The incident took place at around 2.15 pm when the assailants, riding a motorcycle, fired at the CRPF personnel before fleeing the spot, officials said. The injured personnel were shifted to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment.
Here's what we know so far:
CRPF releases statement, says two injured
Post attack, CRPF released a statement confirming that two personnel were injured."Two Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel were injured after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on security personnel deployed at a naka in Kulgam district of Jammu and Kashmir this afternoon. The incident took place at around 2.15 pm when the assailants fired at the CRPF personnel before fleeing the spot.
The injured personnel were shifted to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment," it said.
Recent attack on CRPF personnel in Chhattisgarh
Last month, four CRPF personnel were injured in an accidental explosion while defusing residual explosives at the Alarmedgu camp in Chhattisgarh's Sukma district.The injured personnel belonged to the Ammunition Technician Team of the CRPF's 50th Battalion. They were inspecting camps in the Konta Range and disposing of unserviceable or residual explosives when a fragment of an explosive device detonated.

క్లెయిమ్: 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న జరగనున్న 4వ జాతీయ లోక్ అదాలత్లో పెండింగ్లో ఉన్న ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లను తగ్గించడం/మాఫీ చేయబడతాయి.
ఫాక్ట్: ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లను మాఫీ చేస్తున్నట్లు జాతీయ లేదా రాష్ట్ర లీగల్ సర్వీసెస్ అథారిటీలు ఎక్కడా ప్రకటించలేదు. అయితే, 2026లో కర్ణాటక, బీహార్, ఒడిశా వంటి పలు రాష్ట్రాలు పెండింగ్ చలాన్ల చెల్లింపులో రాయితీని కల్పించాయి. తెలంగాణ, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ రాష్ట్రాలు గతంలో ఇలాంటి రాయితీలు ఇచ్చినప్పటికీ, డిసెంబర్ 2026లో జరగనున్న లోక్ అదాలత్లో మాత్రం ఎలాంటి రాయితీని అధికారికంగా ప్రకటించలేదు. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పుదోవ పట్టించే విధంగా ఉంది.
ముందుగా ఈ విషయం గురించి జాతీయ లోక్ అదాలత్లను నిర్వహించే నేషనల్ లీగల్ సర్వీసెస్ అథారిటీ (NALSA) అధికారిక వెబ్సైట్ను పరిశీలించగా, 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న దేశవ్యాప్తంగా పలు రాష్ట్రాలలో లోక్ అదాలత్లు నిర్వహిస్తున్నట్లు తెలిసింది. దీనిలో భాగంగా విచారణలో ఉన్న సివిల్, క్రిమినల్, చెక్బౌన్స్ కేసులు, కాంపౌండబుల్ ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్ కేసులు, మోటారు వాహన ప్రమాదాలు, కుటుంబ తగాదాలు మొదలైనవాటిని రాజీ మార్గం ద్వారా పరిష్కరించుకునే అవకాశాన్ని ఈ లోక్ అదాలత్లు కల్పిస్తాయి. అయితే, పెండింగ్ ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లను 100% మాఫీ చేయనున్నట్లు ఇందులో ఎక్కడా పేర్కొనలేదు.
ఇదే విషయమై తెలంగాణ స్టేట్ లీగల్ సర్వీసెస్ అథారిటీ (TSLSA) వర్గాలను సంప్రదించగా, 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న తెలంగాణలో జరగనున్న లోక్ అదాలత్లలో ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లకు మాఫీ/ డిస్కౌంట్ ఇస్తున్నట్లు తాము ఎక్కడా అధికారికంగా పేర్కొనలేదని స్పష్టం చేశారు.
అంతేకాకుండా, 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న జరగనున్న లోక్ అదాలత్లలో తెలంగాణ వ్యాప్తంగా పెండింగ్లో ఉన్న ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లను రాయితీపై చెల్లించే అవకాశం కల్పించడం లేదని తెలంగాణ పోలీసులు కూడా మాకు ధృవీకరించారు. మార్చి 2026లో కూడా ఇటువంటి వార్తలే వచ్చినప్పుడు వారు దీన్ని ఖండించారు. మరోవైపు, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ లీగల్ సర్వీసెస్ అథారిటీని, పోలీసులను సంప్రదించగా వారి స్పందించలేదు. అయితే, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ పోలీసులు కూడా పెండింగ్లో ఉన్న ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లపై రాయితీ కల్పించే విషయం గురించి ఎక్కడా అధికారికంగా ప్రకటించలేదు.
అయితే కర్ణాటక, ఒడిశా, బీహార్ వంటి పలు రాష్ట్రాల్లో 2026లో ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లకు రాయితీ కల్పిస్తూ సెటిల్మెంట్ చేసుకునేందుకు వీలుగా ట్రాఫిక్ పోలీసులు లోక్ అదాలత్లను నిర్వహించిన సందర్భాలు ఉన్నాయి. గతంలో హైదరాబాద్ ట్రాఫిక్ పోలీసులు కూడా ఇలాంటి లోక్ అదాలత్లను నిర్వహించారు. 2016, 2017 సంవత్సరాల్లో హైదరాబాద్ ట్రాఫిక్ పోలీసులు గోషామహల్లో లోక్ అదాలత్ నిర్వహించి, 50% రాయితీతో పెండింగ్ చలాన్లను చెల్లించే అవకాశం కల్పించారు. అయితే, 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న జరగనున్న లోక్ అదాలత్లలో తెలంగాణ, ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్ రాష్ట్రాల పోలీసులు లోక్ అదాలత్ ద్వారా ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లపై రాయితీని కల్పించే పథకాన్ని అధికారికంగా ప్రకటించలేదు.
చివరిగా, 12 డిసెంబర్ 2026న జరిగే జాతీయ లోక్ అదాలత్లో పెండింగ్ ట్రాఫిక్ చలాన్లు 100% మాఫీ అవుతాయని సోషల్ మీడియాలో జరుగుతున్న ప్రచారంలో నిజం లేదు.

BSE SME listed Veefin Solutions has migrated to the main board of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the BSE, more than three years after its SME IPO. Veefin's shares opened for trade on the BSE mainboard at ₹249.75 (2.5% higher than previous close) and at ₹250.84 on the NSE. Veefin’s market capitalisation as of 13:20 IST stood at ₹633.76 Cr ($67.61 Mn). Shares of Veefin were trading 1.2% higher at ₹249 apiece on the BSE and 1.2% higher at ₹246.65 apiece on the NSE around 13:30 IST. Veefin listed on the BSE SME platform in July 2023 at ₹86.05, a near 5% premium from its IPO price. The company's ₹46.73 Cr IPO comprised about 57 Lakh shares, with equal parts of fresh issue and offer for sale shares. Its mainboard debut comes on the heels of the company solidifying its financial position over the recent quarter. Its operating revenue for the first half of the ongoing fiscal year (H1 FY27) doubled to ₹238.8 Cr while its consolidated net profit zoomed 127% YoY to ₹24.9 Cr. Veefin reported a 127% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹24.9 Cr in H1 FY27 from ₹11 Cr in the corresponding period last year. Net profit was also up 9% from ₹22.8 Cr in H2 FY26. In Q2 FY27, Veefin's net profit rose 61% sequentially to ₹15.3 Cr from ₹9.5 Cr in the preceding quarter. Operating revenue increased 9% sequentially to ₹124.7 Cr from ₹114.2 Cr, while total income stood at ₹125.7 Cr. The company also reported a deal pipeline of around ₹920 Cr alongside its half-year results. Around 84% of the pipeline comprises opportunities from banks and financial institutions outside India, with Southeast Asia emerging as a key market. The mainboard listing is expected to widen access to Veefin's shares among retail and institutional investors. Unlike the fixed trading lots on the SME platform, the main boards allow investors to buy and sell shares individually. Veefin Bets On AI Employees In a statement, the fintech SaaS company said that it will now look at expanding beyond fintech with an AI platform that enables businesses to deploy digital employees for defined roles. Alongside the listing, the company announced a rebranding from veefin.com to veefin.ai, reflecting the growing role of AI in its products and growth strategy. Its next growth opportunity is through the Veefin AI Operating System (AIOS), a platform designed to help businesses create, deploy and supervise AI employees for defined roles. Veefin has developed more than 1,000 reusable AI skills and has started deploying AIOS internally across three functions: customer implementation, customer support and software testing. The company is using these deployments to improve productivity and build experience before offering the platform to customers. The company sees an opportunity to cross-sell the platform to its current customers and reach enterprises beyond the financial services sector. “We listed on the SME platform three years ago as a supply chain finance technology company. We come to the main boards as a multi-product company whose revenue has more than doubled in the past year, and with many more investors able to take part in what we build next,” Gautam Udani, vice chairperson, cofounder and COO of Veefin Group, said. Founded in 2020 by Udani and Raja Debnath, Mumbai-based Veefin develops lending, supply chain finance and transaction banking software for banks, NBFCs, fintech companies and enterprises. The company began with supply chain finance and has since expanded into trade finance, cash and liquidity management, loan origination, loan management, collections, and corporate and retail digital banking. Its customers use its technology through complete applications, platforms or individual components integrated into their own systems. Veefin has also expanded through acquisitions and strategic investments, including stakes in digital marketing firm White Rivers Media, generative AI startup Walnut AI and lending enablement platform EpikInDiFi. The mainboard transition follows a similar move by E2E Networks, which made its BSE mainboard debut in June after being listed on the NSE since 2018. E2E took the direct listing route to list its shares on the BSE.

Is honesty always the best policy? When to speak up — or stay silent
Never miss a story or episode from Life Kit. Sign up for our weekly newsletter to get our journalism delivered directly to your inbox.
Should you tell your partner how you really feel about their casserole? Offer a colleague feedback about their subpar interview performance? Let a stranger know she has toilet paper on her shoe?
Life Kit
How honest should you really be? Tips for sharing good and bad news
Sometimes the hardest part about talking to other people isn't finding the right words to say — but deciding if you should say anything at all, says social psychologist Vanessa Bohns.
"There are times when honesty is the best policy," she says. "On the other hand, honesty is not the best policy if whatever we say is going to be honest without any instrumental value."
Bohns is the author of Should I Say Something? The Science of What to Share—and What to Keep to Yourself, published in October. The book provides research-backed strategies to help you figure out when to share the truth or a personal opinion. It also offers advice on when to share good news, say sorry or be vulnerable.
There's a reason why giving difficult feedback or even loving criticism can feel like a dilemma. "It pains us to embarrass or hurt other people," Bohns says. So we don't tend to like doing it. In fact, there's a name for the phenomenon — the MUM effect, or minimizing unpleasant messages.
But with care and intention, it's possible to make informed choices about when to speak up or stay quiet, no matter how small or big the situation. Bohns shares three questions to ask yourself before sharing an opinion.
Is this information helpful?
When you decide to tell someone something, remember you're sharing two things: the message itself, and the fact that you are choosing to speak up at all, Bohns says.
People often spend far too much time worrying about the content of their messages, she says. "But the choice of saying something at all communicates so much. It says, 'I see you. I care about your suffering. I want to help you in some way.'"
So, before telling your boss/spouse/mother-in-law how you really feel about that new haircut, Bohn says to consider whether your feedback is actionable.
Honesty is only the best policy if your opinion is going to help someone "perform better or avoid embarrassment or learn something about themselves." If your feedback is mean-spirited, unrelated to the matter at hand or simply can't be enacted, you're probably better off holding your tongue.
For example, flat-out telling your roommate the cake she baked for your birthday tastes terrible? That's just mean. But if she bakes that same cake to enter into a baking competition? It would be mean not to offer her some feedback!
Would I want to hear this?
Just because you don't want to share the truth doesn't mean the person on the receiving end shouldn't or wouldn't want to hear what you have to say.
A 2022 survey, for example, found that people consistently underestimate others' desire for feedback. In the study, researchers put visible smudges of lipstick, chocolate or marker on their faces. Then, without acknowledging those smudges, they went out on the street asking random people to participate in a survey on a different topic.
Less than 3% of the survey participants spoke up, even though the smudges were something the researchers "clearly could have done something about and would have wanted to know," says Bohns.
So, if you choose to stay silent when your new co-worker keeps mispronouncing the name of the company CEO, for example, reflect on your own motivations. "Are you being kind, or are you avoiding your own discomfort?" writes Bohns in her book. Speaking up may help your colleague in this instance.
Do they want your feedback?
Has anyone ever given you advice about a topic you knew more about than they did? Or misjudged how much you knew based on how you looked?
When in doubt, don't assume you know what information the other person wants or needs from you. Pre-assessing how valuable the truth is to someone else, or their ability to handle it, can quickly make well-meaning feedback sound patronizing, writes Bohns in her book.
So just ask the other person if they want the feedback you have to share. "Give them the autonomy, then respect their decision, whatever it might be," she says.

Deadly flash floods hit northern Iraq on Saturday as severe thunderstorms swept across the region, including in neighbouring Iran. The city of Erbil, in Iraq, was particularly badly hit, with extensive damage to homes and businesses. Streets were inundated as torrential rain fell over a short period.
Rainfall exceeded forecasts, with an estimated 80mm falling in the city, compared with expectations of 30mm. Two people were killed in the floods.
In Europe, Storm Bruna is forecast to bring strong winds to Portugal this week, particularly along the west coast. Gusts are expected to reach 50mph (80km/h), with heavy rain and thunderstorms also expected. The total rainfall could reach 200mm by the end of the week. The storm has already affected the Canary Islands, where Tenerife recorded a gust of 80mph on Saturday night.
Japan experienced a cold and snowy end to last week, with further snowfall expected in Hokkaido and parts of the mountains in the main island Honshu.
Temperatures in Japan are forecast to fall below the seasonal average early this week, with Sapporo, the capital of Hokkaido prefecture, expected to plunge to 10C below average. Maximum temperatures in the city are likely to be about 4-6C on Monday and Wednesday, while Tuesday’s high is forecast to be about 0C. Minimum temperatures could fall to -6C by Wednesday, and -8C in other western parts of Hokkaido on Tuesday.
Ski resorts are preparing for visitors after snowfall began on Friday. Total snowfall is expected to reach 30-50cm around Kiroro and Niesko, with about 20-30cm in Furano, Rusutsu and Sapporo.
Other resorts could receive up to 20cm of snow by Wednesday. Strong winds accompanied the snow on Friday and over the weekend, with gusts of about 75mph in Kiroko and Niesko.
During the strong El Niño, sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific were about 3.5C above the climatological average at their peak in late October. As a result, Peru has been experiencing air temperatures 5-10C above the seasonal average. The unusually warm conditions expected to continue into next week.

Google has announced a “super network” upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it’s adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one.
Google’s MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google’s Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel.
With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google’s blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn’t mention either network, saying only that it supports “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks.”
We know one of them is T-Mobile, and the other must be either AT&T or Verizon. When reached for comment, a Google spokesperson declined to name the second network, which is odd. Looking at the Fi coverage map, my best guess for the super network partner is Verizon. The shape of unserved regions is a closer match than AT&T, but carriers do tend to fudge the fine details of these maps.

Keralam: Award-winning farmer held for smuggling drugs hidden in banana bunches
Nair, 31, was arrested in Ernakulam district with 8 grams of MDMA and 803 grams of suspected Hashish oil in his possession
Dhanesh S Nair, aka Dani, a farmer who in 2022 won the award for best young farmer by the state-run Krishi Bhavan in Haripad in Keralam’s Alapuzza district was arrested by police on Monday for allegedly transporting high-value synthetic drugs, including MDMA, concealed inside banana bunches to the state.
“We have learnt that Nair owns banana plantations in Nanjangud near Mysuru in Karnataka. He has been transporting all kinds of synthetic drugs, concealed inside the banana bunches, from Karnataka to Keralam for some time. After bringing the consignments here, he has a network of people to distribute them in several districts of the state,” an officer in Aluva, who was part of the probe told HT.
Nair, 31, was arrested in Ernakulam district with 8 grams of MDMA and 803 grams of suspected Hashish oil in his possession, police said. Police also seized a portion of drugs from a bird feeder at his house.

According to police, Nair was booked under non-bailable sections pertaining to possession of narcotic substances under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and remanded by a magistrate to judicial custody.
Nair’s arrest comes after the arrest and interrogation of two people closely involved with his network, police said.
The two were identified as Harikrishnan KS, who was nabbed from a lodge in Aluva with 185 grams of suspected MDMA, and Shinu Sebastian from Thoppumpady with seven grams of MDMA.
“From a mobile phone seized from them, we got visuals of the drugs being concealed and transported through banana consignments. Both Harikrishnan and Shinu were involved in drug smuggling and supply. They helped him (Nair) transport the drugs to Keralam and also sometimes bought from him and sold them on their own. They were propelled by the high profit margins they were getting,” the officer said.
Police said they received evidence pointing to Nair having links with Nigerian nationals in Bengaluru involved in drug manufacturing and supply. “We have to find out how big his network is in Keralam and how many people worked for him,” the officer said.
Agriculture minister T Siddique said it was shocking that a young award-winning farmer had turned to drug smuggling.
“His acts are an affront to the hardworking farming community. It is shocking that someone with a farming background can be involved in such crimes. I have sought a report from the director of the department on his background,” he said.

Updated - November 09, 2026 02:07 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram
As Keralam grapples with measles outbreaks across districts, particularly Kozhikode, Malappuram and Palakkad, public health experts are calling for a detailed reassessment of the disease’s epidemiology, which appears to have changed significantly over the years.
Once predominantly a childhood disease affecting children aged one to five, measles is now being reported across age groups, including among fully vaccinated individuals and infants below nine months, who are not yet eligible for routine measles vaccination.

- While it is true that the city of Hamtramck, Michigan, approved an ordinance that allows for and regulates religious animal sacrifice, it happened in 2023, not 2026, contrary to online claims.
- Animal sacrifice for religious reasons is expressly permitted in many U.S. cities, and federal law has protections for ritual animal slaughter. A 1993 Supreme Court decision determined a Florida city ordinance banning animal sacrifice was unconstitutional because "a law that explicitly restricts religious practices violates the First Amendment."
- Religious animal sacrifice in Islam — known as Qurban — involves slaughtering and eating livestock like goats and cows during Eid al-Adha, a festival that honors the willingness of the prophet Abraham (or Ibrahim) to sacrifice his son in obedience to God's command.
- Credible reports and estimates suggest that Hamtramck is a majority-Muslim city. However, the U.S. Census does not track religious affiliation and we found no definitive data on the city's religious demographics. The Detroit Free Press, a reputable news outlet, reported that every City Council member in Hamtramck was Muslim in 2023.
- Contrary to the claim's implications, the City Council actually first attempted to expressly ban individual animal slaughter in the city, before reversing course after receiving legal advice and pushback from some in the Muslim community. Both the City Council and Muslim residents of Hamtramck were divided on the ordinance.
In late 2026, a rumor circulated online that Hamtramck, Michigan, a city with an allegedly Muslim-majority population, had recently "legalized animal sacrifice" for religious purposes.
According to these posts, the city's mayor, Amer Ghalib, voted alongside an "all-Muslim city council ... to allow religious animal sacrifice in private homes after the city attorney cited a Supreme Court ruling protecting the practice."
The claim spread across Facebook and X, and Snopes readers asked us to verify whether it was true.
In 2023 — not 2026 — Hamtramck City Council approved an ordinance on a 3-2 vote allowing religious animal sacrifice in private residences, with certain regulations (see the 2:02:15 mark in video of the Jan. 11, 2023, meeting). Ghalib, then the mayor of Hamtramck, also voted in favor, making the final vote 4-2.
While the U.S. Census doesn't track religion, reputable reports suggest Hamtramck became America's first Muslim-majority city in 2013 and had an all-Muslim City Council in 2023.
Thus, we have rated this claim as a mixture of truth, falsehood and undetermined information. It also needs significant context, given that ritual animal sacrifice is allowed in many cities across the United States and it has protections in federal law.
"People might be surprised to know that animal sacrifice is allowed in every city in the state. In fact, the state of Michigan allows it," said the city attorney, Odey Meroueh, during a legal presentation in front of council members (at 1:19:57). "Not only that, but the federal government allows it."
Contrary to the implications of the posts making the claim, Muslim residents and council members were divided on the ordinance, with many actively opposing individual animal slaughter within city limits. (While online posts also claimed the animal-rights group PETA "stayed silent," a PETA official actually appeared on Fox News in 2023 to criticize the City Council's decision.)
Furthermore, it's important to note that unlike the burnt offerings in traditions like that of ancient Greece, religious animal sacrifice in Islam — known as Qurban — simply involves slaughtering and eating livestock like goats and cows during Eid al-Adha, a festival that honors the willingness of the prophet Abraham (or Ibrahim) to sacrifice his son in obedience to God's command.
(While Abraham tied his son Isaac to an altar in mainstream versions of the Bible, in the Quran's version, Abraham's son Ishmael agreed to the sacrifice. God then provided Abraham, who is known as Ibrahim in the Quran, with a ram to sacrifice instead.)
Traditionally, one-third of the meat stays with the family who slaughters the livestock, another third goes to friends and neighbors and the final third is given to people in need.
The ordinance
Hamtramck's city code on animals prohibits the "owning, keeping, or harboring of pigs, horses, cows, sheep, goats, llamas, domestic fowl, outdoor rabbits," unless it is for the "temporary religious sacrificial purposes as permitted by law" (Chapter 90, Section 4).
A separate section in Chapter 90 details regulations for any religious animal sacrifices, which must be done humanely and disposed "in accordance with local, state, and federal law:"
§ 90.030 RELIGIOUS ANIMAL SACRIFICE.
(A) Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to prohibit, abridge or in any way hinder the religious freedom of any person or group. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, ritual handling or other preparation of livestock for ritual slaughter are exempted from the terms of this chapter. For the purposes of this section, the term "ritual slaughter" means slaughter in accordance with the below definition. To conform with the provisions and intent of this chapter, animals not previously rendered insensible, and to be slaughtered in accordance with a humane method as defined in the definition below, shall be slaughtered immediately following total suspension from the floor as otherwise proscribed by city and state law(1) HUMANE METHOD. Means either:(a) A method whereby the animal is rendered insensible to pain by mechanical, electrical, chemical or other means that is rapid and effective, before being shackled, hoisted, thrown, cast or cut; or(b) A method in accordance with ritual requirements of any religious faith whereby the animal suffers loss of consciousness by anemia of the brain caused by the simultaneous and instantaneous severance of the carotid arteries with a sharp instrument.(2) Residents conducting ritual religious sacrifice shall dispose of all waste in accordance with local, state, and federal law.(Ord. 2021-01-10, passed 1-10-2023) Penalty, see § 90.999
Background on the ordinance
According to the Detroit Free Press (archived), the debate began in 2022 after three City Council members attempted to clarify language already in the city's code: 
[Council member Khalil] Refai said the current ordinance already effectively bans slaughter in the city.
But in order to be clear, the subcommittee added the sentence: "No person shall slaughter any animal in the City except for properly licensed commercial facilities in the business of food preparation or police in the course of their duties."
It was that sentence that set off criticism from some in the Muslim community on Facebook, where people organized and spoke out against it.
In response to the outrage, council members struck the proposal to ban slaughter and moved to make revisions that would ensure the right to religious animal sacrifice.
That, too, resulted in controversy. At a 2023 City Council meeting, residents shared concerns about sanitation and worried that children could be traumatized by the slaughter of animals in peoples' backyards. Some also said that they did not want to make their non-Muslim neighbors upset (at 5:41).
Supporters of permitting religious animal sacrifice noted that some in the Jewish community perform animal sacrifices as well, known as kapparot, and have support from their city governments, like in New York (see 50:16). The Free Press reported (archived) that "a group of Orthodox Jews" travel to Hamtramck "every year on the eve of Yom Kippur to slaughter chickens at a halal butcher run by Muslims."
Some supporters also referenced the right to religious freedom in the Constitution and several legal cases.
In 1993, for example, the U.S. Supreme Court determined that a Florida city ordinance banning animal sacrifice was unconstitutional because "a law that explicitly restricts religious practices violates the First Amendment." Meroueh, the city's attorney, also referenced this case in his legal advice.
"Unfortunately, for those who do not want animal sacrifice to proceed, we can't do anything about that. The Supreme Court has already stated that we can't," he said (at 1:24:05).
Ghalib, the mayor, cast his vote in support of the ordinance, "based on legal advice, not based on emotions or self-interest," he said, adding that he would still recommend that people who want to partake in the practice do so outside of the city (see 1:30:52).

Japanese tech investor SoftBank’s Vision Fund 2 (SVF2) booked a valuation loss of $42 Mn on its investment in listed Indian electric vehicle (EV) maker Ola Electric in the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY26 as per the investment firm’s nomenclature). In its investor presentation, SoftBank said that the EV manufacturer’s gross return to the SVF2 stood at $370 Mn in the quarter under review, down $42 Mn (or 10.2%) from $412 Mn in the preceding Q1 FY26. The latest gross return figures are almost 30% lower than $556 Mn that the fund claims to have invested in the OEM so far. In contrast, other listed Indian startups in SVF2’s portfolio – Lenskart and Meesho – together contributed valuation gains worth $394 Mn to the fund’s kitty in Q2 FY26. SoftBank said that the Indian omnichannel eyewear giant helped SVF2 rake in an additional $273 Mn in gross returns during the quarter under review. With this, the fund’s total gross gains from Lenskart stood at $1.3 Bn in Q2 FY26, up 27% sequentially from $1 Bn in preceding quarter. On similar lines, Meesho added another $121 Mn in gains to SVF2’s corpus in the quarter under review. Overall, the Japanese tech giant’s fund sat on gross gains worth $642 Mn on account of the homegrown ecommerce giant in Q2 FY26, up from $521 Mn in the previous quarter. “The investment gain at SVF2 reflected increases in the fair values of certain private portfolio companies due to higher valuations in recent transactions as well as higher share prices of certain public portfolio companies, including Meesho Limited and Lenskart Solutions Limited,” added SoftBank in a statement. SoftBank claims to have so far invested $225 Mn and $285 Mn in Lenskart and Meesho, respectively. Meanwhile, another homegrown SVF2 portfolio startup Swiggy saw a valuation gain of nearly $14 Mn in the quarter under review. The foodtech giant minted gross returns worth $451 Mn in Q2 FY26 (up from $437 Mn in Q1 FY26) against a total investment of $450 Mn. However, the road was not so smooth for listed Indian startups in Vision Fund 1 (SVF1). The fund booked a sequential valuation loss of $34 Mn on account of Delhivery in Q2 FY26. Against a gross return of $701 Mn in Q1 FY26, the logistics giant ended the September 2026 quarter with an even lower gross return of $667 Mn. Similarly, SoftBank pegged the gross return on its investment in FirstCry parent BrainBees Solutions at $308 Mn in the quarter under review, down 14% or $50 Mn, from $358 Mn in Q1 FY26. Overall, SoftBank swung to the red and posted a net loss of nearly $7 Bn in Q2 FY26 against a profit of $15.9 Bn in the year ago period. This was its first loss-making quarter in nearly two years as the company was hit by rising buildout costs for data centres in the US and a sharp jump in financing payments. The investment firm also reported $14.1 Bn in net sales in the quarter under review, up 15.6% from $12.2 Bn in Q2 FY25. SoftBank is one of the major foreign investors in the country and has so far deployed nearly $16 Bn in Indian startups. Having funded nearly a fifth of India’s 100+ unicorns, SoftBank has previously backed the likes of Flipkart, OYO, Delhivery, OfBusiness, FirstCry and Meesho.

The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal.
Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost.
Reeves accused Argentina of surreptitiously seeking to pursue its longstanding sovereignty claims over the south Atlantic islands through an application to the tribunal, which is sitting over two days in Hamburg.
Argentina is seeking a provisional ruling suspending the drilling for oil before further arbitration over the future of the project, which it claims poses an environmental risk.
Reeves told the tribunal: “In reality, what Argentina opposes is hydrocarbon activities for the economic benefit of the Falkland Islanders. What it wants is to take control of those resources for itself.”
Argentina claims Britain’s approval of the Sea Lion project is in breach of a 1976 UN resolution calling on both parties to desist from unilateral action on the islands until the sovereignty dispute is settled.
Buenos Aires wants to force a commitment from the UK that it will “stop the drilling”, in order to “preserve the present situation” before a settlement over the oilfield.
After raising Argentina’s “armed invasion” of the islands in 1982, which she told the tribunal led to “loss of life and military occupation”, Reeves said the Falkland Islanders had a right to exploit their own natural resources, adding that a tribunal that ruled over the law of the seas had no place in settling a sovereignty dispute.
Reeves said that suspension of the drilling, which is due to start in March next year, would kill off the Sea Lion project.
“The provisional measures sought by Argentina would prevent the people of the Falkland Islands from developing their natural resources as they are entitled to do so, pursuant to their fundamental right to self-determination,” she said.
“The measures sought would have devastating consequences for the Falklands people. They risk losing billions of pounds in money, which is essential for the islands’ economic development.”
Sir Michael Wood KC, who also spoke on behalf of the UK, said the tribunal could lose member states should it overreach by issuing “provisional” measures that should be used only in exceptional circumstances.
Asked whether the UK would abide by the tribunal’s ruling, Reeves told the Guardian that she respected the institution but that she would not “get ahead” of the decisions.
Speaking earlier on Tuesday, Mario Oyarzábal, chief legal adviser to Argentina’s ministry of foreign affairs, had told the tribunal that the 3,600 inhabitants of the Falkland Islands, had no right to the resources around the south Atlantic archipelago.
Oyarzábal said: “[Argentina] respects the interests of the inhabitants of the islands and their way of life as enshrined in the Argentine constitution … What these British citizens do not have is a right to decide to which state the islands belong …
“These resources belong to the Argentine people. Some 46 million of them including the 1,247 inhabitants born on the islands whose interests will be duly taken into account.”
He said Argentina was ready to negotiate “all aspects of the question” of the Falkland Islands, which are known as the Malvinas in Argentina, “including the present aggravation of the dispute caused by the UK”.
He accused the UK of refusing to enter talks over the islands while pushing forward on the exploitation of its natural resources in a way that would entrench the status quo.
Oyarzábal claimed that the oil money from the drilling would “finance the very military base and presence that sustains the UK’s de facto control of the territory”.
Argentina’s case is that provisional measures to suspend the drilling are urgent. The Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin, led by the Israeli firm Navitas and its British partner, Rockhopper, will start drilling in March and oil will be extracted from 2028 and continue for 35 years. It has the potential to double the islands’ GDP per capita to a cumulative uplift of £8bn over the lifetime of the project. The UK government asked why an application to Itlos had only been made in recent months amid increasingly bellicose rhetoric.
Argentina further claims that it has rights as the “coastal state” to the Falklands. The UK’s lawyers said this claim highlighted that Argentina’s application was “at heart” about sovereignty.
The Sea Lion project has been condemned as unlawful by Argentina’s president, Javier Milei. The tribunal was told by Argentinian lawyers that the permissions given by the UK government for drilling was the “unilateral conduct” of a “colonial power”.
Oyarzábal added: “In the event of a blowout or spill, it is Argentina that would bear its consequences and be called upon to respond, not a state that is 12,700km away.”
UK lawyers responded that the risk of such an incident was low and that the companies involved had mitigated against it.
Argentina invaded the Falklands in 1982 at the cost of the lives of 649 Argentinian military personnel, 255 British military personnel and three Falkland Islanders. The hearing is the first time that substantive matters relating to the islands have been litigated at an international tribunal. In a show of solidarity, Princess Anne arrived in Port Stanley on Monday. The hearing continues on Wednesday.

Quick Answer
You can run AI models locally on Android and iPhone using Google AI Edge Gallery or PocketPal AI, and on Mac and Windows using LM Studio or Ollama. Simply install the app, download a compatible AI model, and start using it offline. Your data stays on your device, with no cloud access required after setup.
While many think AI is a bubble that is going to burst one day, it might be true, or it might not be at all. Only time will tell. But we should all accept that AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with our devices and do work.
For me, my life revolves around AI: I hand off some of my work to it and do things that once weren’t possible.
AI models are rapidly evolving. If you don’t know what an AI model is, it powers the apps and interfaces you interact with. For instance, the ChatGPT app uses GPT models, and the Claude app is powered by Claude models, which run behind the scenes.
While AI is fundamentally changing how we interact with devices and making work easier, handing your sensitive data to it has remained a major privacy concern.But thanks to rapid AI model development, many capable, powerful AI models enough to run locally on your device, without your data leaving your device
Companies like Google and Meta offer free AI models that can run locally on most consumer devices, including your mobile phone. Apps like Google’s AI Edge Gallery and PocketPal AI also make it easy to discover and run AI models locally without technical expertise.
If you have a capable computer with decent RAM, you can also run AI models locally to use them for writing your email, summarising PDFs, data analysis, coding, using their vision capabilities, and much more.
However, setting up an AI model locally involves downloading the app, choosing the model yourself, and understanding its capabilities first.
To help you out, I have created this detailed, comprehensive guide to set up and run local AI models on your device on Android, iPhone, Mac, or even on Windows.
I wrote this guide with beginners in mind, so every step is comprehensive and easy to follow. If you have questions, comment below. I am happy to help you. Most of these models can run locally on many consumer applications, but before that, don’t forget to check our prerequisites because that’s where your journey starts.
Table of Contents
Pre-Requirements To Run AI Models Locally on Device
Your device’s RAM determines whether it can run AI models.
Technically, a model loads into your RAM to run. As a general rule of thumb, a model needs about as much free RAM as its download size.
So, more RAM leaves room to run large AI models. A minimum of 6 GB of RAM is required to run decent, capable AI models locally on your device
Similarly, you need enough storage to download and store models locally. A model can generally range from 2 GB to 20 GB or even more, depending on its size and capabilities.
Finally, you need an internet connection and enough data to download the model so you can run it offline.
As I said before, these models can range from 2 GB to 20 GB. So it requires an internet connection to download the model and store it locally on your device.
Of course, Other minimum specifications, such as a capable Processor, Operating system, and platform, also matter but not as much as RAM does.
How to check how much RAM your device has
On Android:
Go to About Device to see how much RAM your smartphone has. To do that: Open Settings on your device, tap on the search bar at the top, and search for “About Device”. On some phones, scroll down and tap “About Device”. Look at the RAM specifications.
On some phones, you will see extra visible RAM after the plus sign, for example, 16GB + 12GB. However, only the first number is the real memory.
iPhone:
Apple generally doesn’t disclose the RAM used in iPhones. However, iPhone 15 Pro and newer devices generally have at least 8GB, while older iPhones have less than 6GB, which can run 1 billion to 2 billion models. You can check how much RAM your iPhone has from here.
Mac:
To check how much RAM on your MacBook: From the home screen, click on the Apple icon in the top left corner screen and tap on About This Mac. From here, you can check chip and memory options. Apple MacBooks running on Apple Silicon are especially good for running local AI models since the graphics chip shares all the memory.
Windows:
On Windows, you can go to Settings > System > About. From there, check the installed RAM, graphics card, and system type (x86 or ARM-based), which determines which applications you can download to run AI models locally.
Once your device meets the minimum RAM requirement, follow these steps to set it up to run AI models locally. Use the table of contents above to go to the device you want to set up. This guide covers Android, iPhone, Mac, and Windows.
How to Run AI Models Locally on Any Device
Android:
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on Android with Google AI Edge Gallery
You can run Google’s family of Open-weight AI models locally for free on your Android device using Google’s own AI Edge Gallery app (Free).
Gemma 4 is Google’s latest open-weight model. It comes in five model sizes. Gemma 4 E2B and Gemma 4 E4B are suitable for running on Android devices. 2B requires at least 8GB of RAM, and 4B requires at least 12GB of RAM.
Gemma 4 also supports vision capabilities, so it is not just text; you can also use it to understand images.
How to install and run the latest Google Gemma 4 models locally on your Android phone
Step 1: Download Google AI Edge Gallery from the Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI Chat.
Step 3: Under the recommended models, tap Download below. To download the model you want. Gemma 4 E2B is 2.6 GB and best for starters, while Gemma 4 E4B is 3.7 GB and smarter, but your phone needs at least 8 GB of RAM to run it locally.
Step 3: Once the model is downloaded, tap Try it.
Step 4: Type your prompt in the Type prompt box and tap the send button.
Step 5: Like the other AI apps, the model replies to your prompt. You can also see how fast the model runs, measured in tokens per second, and how much RAM it uses. On my Android phone, the Gemma 4 E2B model ran at about 30 tokens per second, and my model comes with 16 GB of RAM.
Method 2: Run any open model on Android with PocketPal AI
PocketPal is a popular free and open-source app for running AI models locally on Android.
Unlike Google’s AI Edge Gallery, it supports a wide variety of third-party models, including Google’s Gemma, Meta’s Llama, Microsoft’s Phi, Qwen, and more. It also supports GGUF models, including compressed versions.
How do I use the PocketPal app to run AI models locally on my device?
Step 1: Download and install the PocketPal app from the Google Play Store. Here is the direct download link.
Step 2: Open the app and, during onboarding, tap Download Model.
Step 3: Pick any available model to download and tap Download,
or tap the plus option to find more. To get a new model, tap the plus icon, select Hugging Face, then tap Choose and add from Hugging Face.
Step 4: From here, you can search for any model. In this case, I searched for the Qwen3 1.7B parameter model and tapped the download icon to download it locally.
Step 5: Once done, open the Models tab and select the model to load it. Now go to the chat interface and enter the prompt, and the model uses the model that you have loaded, in this case, the Qwen3 1.7 billion parameter model, to answer your queries. You can also see how much time it takes to run this model on your device.
iPhone
Method 1: Run Gemma 4 on iPhone with Google AI Edge Gallery
Google’s AI Edge Gallery is also available on iPhone and supports the latest Gemma 4 family of open-weight models, similar to Android. You can download and use E2B (around 2.6 GB) and the E4B model (around 3.7 GB).
Apple doesn’t disclose the RAM used on iPhones. However, the latest iPhone models, including the iPhone 15 Pro and later, support up to 8 GB of RAM, which can run these models faster and more reliably. However, older iPhones may struggle with slow responses, battery drain, and overheating, so keep that in mind.
Step 1: Download the Google AI Edge Gallery app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app and tap on AI chat
Step 3: Now download the compatible AI model. In this case, I’m downloading Gemma 4 E2B, which is about 2.59 GB. Click on the download icon under the model.
Step 4: Wait for the model to download, then tap Try It, enter the prompt, and wait for a reply. If you want to use the vision capabilities, tap on the plus icon and upload an image
Method 2: Run open models on iPhone with PocketPal AI
Similar to Google’s AI Edge Gallery app, the PocketPal app is also available on iPhone. It also gives access to some of the popular Hugging Face model library and other third-party models, including models from Meta, Cohere, and more. It also supports Google Gemma 4 models.
Step 1: Install the PocketPal AI app on your iPhone. Here is the link.
Step 2: Open the app, tap Download Model, select a model, and tap Download. In this case, I am downloading the Qwen3 1.7B model.
Step 3: Once downloaded, tap the Load option at the top, enter the prompt, and wait for the reply
Mac
Method 1: Run AI models on a Mac with LM Studio
You can use LM Studio on Mac to run AI models locally.
It supports a wide range of models, including models from Google Gemma, Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, and more. Like the mobile app, you can install LM Studio on your Mac, download a model, and start chatting. It also supports GGUF and Apple-optimized MLX models.
Depending on the model, you can have text conversations, image analysis, and more. You can also use it as a local API for other apps.
However, LM Studio is only available on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or later). Intel Macs are not supported.
How to install and run AI models locally using LM Studio on Mac
Step 1: First, go to lmstudio.ai/download and download the LM Studio app for Mac. Select the compatible version and drag and drop LM Studio into Applications to install it.
Step 2: Open LM Studio on the Mac, click on the model search in the sidebar, and search for the model; for example, in this case, I searched for the Gemma 4 E4B model
Step 3: You can also pick a different model, select it, and click Download. A likely fit badge here means that it is suitable to run locally on your Mac using your Mac’s available memory. Once the model is downloaded, tap on Use in the new chat instead.
Step 4: On the home screen, click Load Model in the dialog and select the model. You can also raise the context length here if you are planning for long conversations.
Step 5: Now enter the prompt and press Enter. The model returns with an option. You can also click the model server in the sidebar and turn on the status to use the model for other apps via an OpenAI-compatible API at http://localhost:1234.
Method 2: Run AI models on a Mac with Ollama
You can also run AI models on your Mac using Ollama. It is a free, lightweight tool by Meta that lets you run local AI models in the terminal with one command. It also works with many local apps that support local AI.
Step 1: To run Ollama locally on your device, go to ollama.com/download and click on the Download manually option. You can also directly paste the command into the terminal if you are a developer.
Step 2: Next, open the Ollama.dmg, drag it into Applications, and open it
Step 3: On the onboarding screen, while setting up an account, Ollama asks you to sign up for an account; however, you can tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally’
Step 4: Next, to run ollama run llama3, copy the ollama run llama3 command, open Terminal, and paste it. Wait for the model to download completely. Ollama can run Qwen3 4B parameters and other models. In this case, I am going to run the Ollama run Qwen3 4B model. So, wait for the model to download completely.
Step 5: Finally, you can start using the Ollama model right there. You can enter the prompt directly, and it will reply in the same terminal.
Windows
Method 1: Run AI models on Windows with LM Studio
You can use the same LM Studio on Windows as well to run AI models locally on your device
Step 1: Download and install LM Studio for Windows. Here is the download page link.
Step 2: Open the LM Studio app and, in the left sidebar, tap Model Search and search for the model you want to run locally. In this case, Iam using Qwen3 1.7 billion parameters; on the model details page, click the download option.
Step 3: Wait for it to download, and once it has downloaded, tap on Use in new chat
Step 4: Now, on the home screen, in the model box, select the downloaded model. You can tap on the model to select and enable it, then enter the prompt and press enter.
Method 2: Run AI models on Windows with Ollama
Ollama is also available on Mac. It supports NVIDIA and AMD graphics cards, as well as the latest ARM-based Snapdragon PCs. You can download models and use them directly from the terminal. Here is how.
Step 1: First, download Ollama on Windows. Go to ollama.com/download/windows and click Manual download. If you are a developer, you can install it directly in PowerShell using the PowerShell command.
Step 2: Now install the Ollama app on Windows. While setting up, click Continue, and then tap on No thanks, I will use Ollama locally, so you can skip creating an account.
Step 3: Next, copy the command shown in the app, open Terminal, and run this command: ollama run qwen3:1.7b, and press Enter. It downloads the model. Wait for the download to complete.
Step 4: Now enter your question and press Enter.
This is how you can set up and run AI models locally on Android, iPhone, Windows, and Mac. Choosing the right model is important to get high-quality output. Bigger models don’t always mean better outputs, as their capabilities can vary. Our guide to the best AI models to run locally should help you choose the right model for your needs. If you have any issues setting them up, feel free to comment below, and I’ll be happy to help.

In Brazil, they rallied online by the millions, sharing videos and spreading memes. In Serbia, they cycled across Europe and ran ultramarathons to make their voices heard.
Both movements burst into international public view last month as they became central during election campaigns to the pushback against authoritarianism. What they also offered, however, was a window into a wider phenomenon playing out across the globe, as youth-led movements reshape political landscapes.
“Gen Z is rising,” said Erica Chenoweth, a political scientist at Harvard Kennedy School. “It is abundantly clear that a significant proportion of gen Z is tired of sitting on the sidelines while their political systems fail them.”
Researchers have documented at least 25 protests around the world in which this age group – roughly those between the ages of 14 and 29 – has played a role.
From Bangladesh to Belgium and Italy to India, it seems gen Z, who account for about a third of the world’s population, have found their voice. “Gen Z may be experiencing a global political awakening,” Chenoweth wrote in a recent essay.
Their reasons for taking to the streets have varied widely, from protesting against corruption and an unequal playing field to calling for more investment in education, affordable housing and action on the climate crisis.
Many of the first protests to make waves were in Asia and Africa. In 2024, students in Dhaka, Bangladesh, made global headlines after they pulled off what was described as the world’s first successful gen Z-led revolution.
The protests began over a quota law but swiftly snowballed into a wider show of discontent against the increasingly autocratic rule of the prime minister, Sheikh Hasina. Two months later, Hasina resigned and fled the country by helicopter after being, as the Associated Press reported, “chased out by young protesters”.
Two years later and 4,000 miles away, students were at the helm of another revolution in Serbia, pushing back against a government that had steadily tightened its grip on the media and stuffed institutions with party loyalists.
Late last month, Serbia’s students’ movement was catapulted from the streets to the halls of power as they ousted Aleksandar Vučić in elections, bringing an end to his party’s 14 years in power.
Students and young people have long been at the forefront of the push for change, the analysts Cait Dallaire and Sebastian Dittgen wrote recently, citing the US civil rights movement and the 2011 Arab spring.
“What is unique about the current movement is the infrastructure of mobilisation: TikTok and X amplify and accelerate grievances; Discord servers and group chats enable decentralised planning; virtual private networks and mirrored content help organisers circumvent internet shutdowns,” they said.
It was this potent combination – young people in the streets and social media – that helped drive Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s comeback to win Brazil’s presidential election last month. After a bruising loss in the first round to the rightwing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, there was dismay in the country’s political left.
That was until students from the Fluminense Federal University mobilised in a pro-Lula march, setting off a wave of similar actions across the country. Soon after, the congressman and Lula ally André Janones, 42, created a WhatsApp channel called “Lula’s Army” that attracted millions of people looking to help boost pro-Lula content on social media.
On the night of his victory, Lula recognised their power. “I want to thank the generosity of Brazil’s young people who took to the streets to defend democracy,” he said.
Some politicians have sought to engage gen Z from the start. In the US, Zohran Mamdani’s campaign for New York mayor combined a canny use of social media with a legion of about 50,000 volunteers that had young people at its heart. The New York Times wrote that “volunteering for Mr Mamdani’s campaign became a salve” for young New Yorkers as the campaign became not just about “mobilising, but socialising”.
It was a nod to the global context in which many gen Zers have come of age; one riven by conflicts such as the Israel-Gaza war, the escalating climate crisis and the rise of nationalism, while the rules that have shaped the international order since the second world war are fraying.
In recent weeks, youth-led protests have begun to sweep Europe, from school students in France demanding better conditions in which to work to those in Spain who pitched tents to rally for affordable housing. In Germany, thousands of people took to the streets to protest against the cost of living and call for more investment in education, health and climate action in a movement organised by a group calling itself Gen Z regelt!, or Gen Z will sort this.
Analysts have been swift to point to the link between the protests. “The reasons are different, but they share the same spark: the breakdown of the social contract,” Arancha González, the dean of the Paris School of International Affairs, told the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera. “In Europe, the idea that economies generate wellbeing and social equality has been shattered.”
A similar note of disillusionment threads through India’s Cockroach movement, which began as an online satire and has since swelled into a show of force against the strongman government of Narendra Modi. Fuelled by social media and rooted in democratic ideals, the power of the movement was laid bare this summer after Cockroach-led protests forced the resignation of the country’s education minister.
Equally visible is the pushback by India’s security forces against the movement, detaining thousands, unleashing teargas and beating people with lathis, or wooden clubs. Authorities went to extreme lengths in October to keep them from gathering in central Delhi, barricading roads and shutting down the internet and public transport.
It was a window into another facet that has defined youth-led protests, as research suggests they tend to be met with higher levels of repression, despite the fact that they are no more likely to use violence than others.
In France, lawyers and rights groups say several teenagers have suffered war-like injuries from police weapons. After the 2024 protests in Bangladesh, UN human rights experts said as many as 1,400 people had been killed, mostly by security forces, while thousands more suffered severe, often life-altering injuries.
In a recent analysis, Civicus, a non-profit that monitors global civic freedoms, said: “Because they question the distribution of economic and political power, gen Z-led protests have invariably been met with state violence,” linking the violence meted out to young protesters with their focus on systems and institutions that have long been generally accepted.
In Morocco, more than 2,000 people were charged and many received harsh prison sentences after a 2025 movement known as Gen Z 212 targeted officials over corruption, neglected public services and the lack of opportunities. Weeks later, in Mexico, youth-led protests over corruption and crime led to clashes with police in which dozens of people were arrested.
The outcomes of both of these movements show the varying success of gen Z protests. But at times, the foundations laid in one protest have given rise to others. In the US, much of today’s youth organising was shaped by the pro-Palestine student movement, in which there were thousands of arrests, expulsions and suspensions. Many schools instated anti-protest policies amid a broader rollback of educational freedom on campus.
Students, however, have continued to push for change. Last month hundreds in North Carolina marched in the heat to the polls after their historically Black university was denied a polling site, while thousands across the country have responded to the Cornell 7 case by skipping class, protesting and launching occupations.
As Chenoweth of the Harvard Kennedy School noted, the wave of recent youth-led protests may mark the beginning of a “profound generational transformation in world affairs” – one that could be capable of countering the global trend of democratic backsliding.
Ultimately, however, as Bilal Narjissi, a 17-year-old high school student in a suburb north of Paris recently told the Associated Press, the explosion of youth movements across Europe hints at a wider truth that has long been overlooked across the globe.
“We all agree on one point,” he said. “That young people are treated like children, far too much, and that they aren’t listened to enough.”

దీపావళి సందర్భంగా పంజాబ్ నేషనల్ బ్యాంకు, ఎయిర్టెల్ వంటి సంస్థలు వినియోగదారులకు ₹2000 నగదును కానుకగా ఇస్తున్నాయని సోషల్ మీడియాలో కొన్ని పోస్టులు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) ప్రచారంలో ఉన్నాయి. ఈ నగదును పొందేందుకు, పోస్టులో ఉన్న లింకును క్లిక్ చేయాలంటూ అందులో పేర్కొనబడింది. దీనిలో ఎంత నిజముందో ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: దీపావళి కానుకగా పంజాబ్ నేషనల్ బ్యాంకు, ఎయిర్టెల్ సంస్థలు ₹2000 నగదును ప్రజలకు ఇస్తున్నాయి.
ఫాక్ట్: పంజాబ్ నేషనల్ బ్యాంకు, ఎయిర్టెల్ సంస్థలు అధికారికంగా ఇలాంటి ఆఫర్లు ఏవీ ప్రకటించలేదు.ఇవి కేవలం ప్రజల వ్యక్తిగత వివరాలను, డబ్బులను దొంగిలించడానికి సైబర్ నేరగాళ్లు సృష్టించిన నకిలీ (ఫిషింగ్) వెబ్సైట్లు. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పు.
ముందుగా, పంజాబ్ నేషనల్ బ్యాంకు, ఎయిర్టెల్ సంస్థలు ఇటువంటి ఆఫర్ ఏమైనా ప్రకటించారా అని వెతకగా, వారి అధికారిక వెబ్సైట్లు, సోషల్ మీడియా ఖాతాల్లో (ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) ఎక్కడా కూడా వినియోగదారులకు దీపావళి కానుకగా డబ్బులు ఇస్తున్నట్లు వెల్లడించలేదు. పైగా, తమ సంస్థల పేరును వాడుకొని లింకులు, యాప్లను పంపి సైబర్ నేరగాళ్లు ప్రజలను మోసం చేస్తున్నారని, అందువలన అనుమానాస్పద లింక్లను క్లిక్ చేయవద్దని గతంలోనే వారు పలుమార్లు(ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) హెచ్చరించారు.
ఇక, వైరల్ అవుతున్న లింకులను పరిశీలించగా, అవి ఈ రెండు సంస్థలకు చెందినవి కావని, అనుమానాస్పద డొమైన్ పేర్లతో ఉన్న ఫిషింగ్ వెబ్సైట్లుగా చూడవచ్చు. ఇందులో ఇవ్వబడిన కామెంట్లు కూడా నిజమైనవి కావు, వినియోగదారులను నమ్మించడానికి ఇటువంటి కామెంట్లను సైబర్ నేరగాళ్లు సృష్టిస్తారు. ఈ వెబ్సైట్లు ఫోన్ నంబర్ వంటి వ్యక్తిగత వివరాలను సేకరిస్తాయి. తద్వారా, భవిష్యత్తులో మరిన్ని సైబర్ నేరాలకు ఈ వ్యక్తిగత సమాచారాన్ని వాడుకుంటారు.
అలాగే, భారత ప్రభుత్వం కూడా ప్రజలకు దీపావళి కానుకగా డబ్బు ఇస్తుందని కొన్ని లింకులు (ఆర్కైవ్) ప్రచారంలో ఉన్నాయి. ఇవి కూడా పూర్తిగా మోసపూరితమైనవని గతంలో మేము ఫ్యాక్ట్-చెక్ ఆర్టికల్ ప్రచురించాం. సైబర్ క్రైమ్ విభాగాలు కూడా వీటి పైన ఎప్పటికప్పుడు ప్రజలకు అవగాహన కల్పిస్తూ, ఇటువంటి మోసపూరిత సమాచారాన్ని నమ్మవద్దని, అధికారిక సమాచారాన్ని మాత్రమే అనుసరించాలని పేర్కొంటున్నారు.
చివరిగా, పంజాబ్ నేషనల్ బ్యాంకు, ఎయిర్టెల్ సంస్థల పేరుతో ప్రచారంలో ఉన్న ఈ దీపావళి ఆఫర్లు ఫేక్.

The West Bengal Police on November 5 posted a message on X, calling for citizens to celebrate Diwali responsibly. The AI-generated poster showed a stray dog and two cats taking shelter from firecrackers. It said, “Please celebrate responsibly. It’s our Diwali too!”
The post, which was made at 8:29 am, was however taken down within 3 hours. (Archive)
In recent years, campaigns highlighting the environmental impact of firecrackers and calling for restrictions during Diwali have increasingly been framed by a section of the Right wing as an affront to Hindu religious sentiments. The issue of air pollution, consequently, has often been recast as a communal debate, with calls for curbs on firecrackers portrayed as selective targeting of Hindu festivals.
In the same vein, several social media users took offence to Bengal police’s awareness post, claiming that it was a case of selective bias against Hindus. Users began commenting under the post, some of whom went as far as to tag chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, questioning why similar awareness campaigns were allegedly absent during Eid and Christmas.
Some of the comments are displayed in the gallery below. (A few of them contain abusive words. Reader discretion is advised).
Following the backlash, the post was deleted. West Bengal police offered no explanation or clarification as to why the post was removed. Many had anticipated that the West Bengal Police would backtrack on its awareness campaign as this incident forms part of a pattern of state authorities taking down posts on firecracker awareness ahead of Diwali following backlash.
Pattern of Deletion
Alt News had earlier reported that on October 25, Delhi Police had deleted an X post, which raised awareness about a cracker-free Diwali, within hours of posting it. On that occasion, too, social media users had predicted that the post would be removed soon.
Again, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) removed a similar video featuring actress Dia Mirza advocating for a pollution-free Diwali from its social media handles. Both decisions came in the wake of social media outrage from BJP-RSS supporters that these posts hurt the religious sentiments of Hindus. Justice G S Kulkarni of the Bombay high court then directed BMC to re-upload Mirza’s video, remarking “She (Dia Mirza) rendered a really really good message in terms of air pollution… These (opposing Mirza) are stray thoughts of very few people and we should avoid them…”
A video uploaded by AISA president Neha Bora calling for an environment-friendly Diwali was likewise condemned by the Hindutva brigade.
On November 4, actress Soni Razdan’s social media advocacy for a pollution-free Diwali was also derided by several users. “People can’t understand a simple message because they think every statement is about religion,” she retorted to an X post that had targeted her.
Then you are simply unable to see the woods for the trees. It’s not bursting crackers that is anti-national. What is anti national is the fact that you are contributing to the terrible air pollution. My goodness. No wonder we all can’t breathe. People can’t understand a simple message because they think every statement is about religion. It’s not. It’s about AIR. And children are struggling. So to make it simple for you – it is the irresponsible actions of people that seem to be anti national. To me. And should also be to you. Because it’s your children, everyone’s children irrespective of which religion they belong to., that are suffering. And so are the citizens of this country. I’m assuming that also includes you.
— Soni Razdan (@Soni_Razdan) November 5, 2026
Alt News also found that the official X handle of West Bengal Police had made similar awareness campaigns around Diwali, in both 2024 and 2025. These posts still exist.

Rosemary Nyirumbe became a nun when she was just in her mid-teens – and she felt her true vocation lay in rehabilitating children who had been through some of the worst trauma imaginable. So that’s what she did. In this episode Mike Wooldridge hears Sr Rosemary’s astonishing story. The feared rebel group, the Lord’s Resistance Army, started to terrorise the north of Uganda in the 1980s. Many children, girls as well as boys, were abducted and forced to become child soldiers. In many cases, the LRA forced them to commit atrocities, leaving them deeply traumatised. Many of the girls also bore the children of rebel leaders. As they started to return home, these children were often rejected by their families and communities, says Sr Rosemary. So she set about giving them a future and a hope: through enabling them to acquire skills like sewing, and by helping them see that God had not rejected them for the atrocities they had been forced to commit. More than once, Sr Rosemary put herself in enormous danger in order to fulfil her mission. But, she says, she also learnt that small acts of kindness can touch the hearts of even battle-hardened rebels.
