If your Android phone’s battery drains too quickly, try enabling auto-brightness, using dark mode, limiting background apps, reducing screen timeout, and turning off unused features. These 15 practical tips can improve battery life and help maintain battery health.
I cannot function without my phone. It makes my experience better during my walks, jogs, and all other activities throughout the day. Unfortunately, I have to charge my phone multiple times a day or keep a power bank as a backup, just in case. The ease created by my Android phone is instantly undone by the quickly draining battery. Along with the phone, I should carry a cable, an adapter, and a power bank.
In that frustration, I started looking into why my Android phone battery was draining fast. I checked the battery usage data, identified what was causing the drain, and fixed those issues. Now, my battery lasts longer. These are the tips that helped me improve the battery life on my Android phone.
Table of Contents
Android Phone Battery Draining Fast? Try These 10 Tips
I used these tips to improve my Android phone’s battery life on a single charge. You can use the tips that work for you without sacrificing the functionality you need.
Enable Auto Brightness
Brightness affects how visible the display is, irrespective of the light in our surroundings. When we keep the brightness too high, it affects our eyes in the dark. In addition to that, the battery drains too quickly when powering the high brightness for your phone’s display.
If we keep the brightness low, it affects the visibility of our phone’s display during daytime when we are out in the open under the sun. To not affect the visibility and save the battery from draining quickly, we can enable Auto Brightness on our phone.
The auto-brightness feature on our phones adjusts the brightness of our display based on the light in our surroundings. For example, when you are outside where there is abundant sunlight, the auto-brightness feature increases the brightness to make visibility better for you. Similarly, it decreases the brightness when you are in a dark or dimmed environment.
To enable auto-brightness on your phone, open the Settings app and go to Display or Display & brightness settings. The jargon for options varies by manufacturer.
Find Brightness options and toggle the button beside Auto brightness to enable it. You will see the brightness of your screen increase or decrease as per your environment in real time.
Enable Dark Mode
Android phones with OLED or AMOLED displays consume more power for display. If it is set to light mode, a major chunk of battery life goes to power. Setting the screen to dark mode makes it easier on the battery. The battery does not need to power the entire display by switching off the black pixels.
You can enable dark mode in the display settings of your phone. Open the Settings app and find the display settings. Set the display mode to Dark mode.
Dark mode, at first, may look odd. Once you get accustomed to it, there is no going back.
Disable Always-On Display
Always-On Display consumes a significant amount of power from the battery. The display always shows time or notifications even when you are not using the phone actively.
You must disable the Always-On Display feature if you do not have any use for it. Open the Settings app on your Android phone and search for Always-On Display. It will show the option. Tap on it. Toggle the button beside Always-On Display to turn it off.
It may not reduce battery drain noticeably, but small things like these can help optimize battery life.
Set Screen Refresh Rate to Auto
The screen refresh rate feature on Android gives us a smoother display experience. Manufacturers flaunt the screen refresh rate while launching and advertising new smartphones. The higher the refresh rate of a screen is, the more battery it consumes. If you are not a gamer or do not use your phone for experiences that demand a higher refresh rate, you may set the Screen refresh rate to Auto.
Open the Settings app on your phone, search for refresh rate, and open the refresh rate options. Then, set the refresh rate to Auto or Auto-select. Instead of using a higher refresh rate that consumes more battery, your phone now optimizes the screen refresh rate based on the app or activity for a smoother experience. You may also set it to Standard or anything that offers a 60 Hz refresh rate to extend battery life.
If you are a gamer, Auto refresh rate would be the best option.
Decrease Screen Off Time
Screen off time is something we mostly overlook when looking to optimize battery on our phones. If the screen off time is set to a longer time, it consumes battery and aids in draining faster. Small things like these add up and drain the battery.
Open the Settings app on your phone and search for screen off. You can find the Screen off feature in Display settings. Tap on the Screen off or Auto Screen off options (based on your manufacturer) and select a shorter time.
Now, when you do not use the phone, the screen will be turned off as per the time you have selected. The shorter the time, the more you optimize the battery.
Disable Unnecessary Sounds and Vibrations
Sound and vibration for ringtones and notifications are okay. But touch vibrations, keyboard sounds, dial pad tones, lock sounds, and other such sounds or vibrations when we do something on our phone are not necessary. They stress the battery and make it drain faster.
Disabling those unnecessary sounds and vibrations enhances the battery life and saves you from charging the phone frequently.
Open the Settings app on your phone and go to Sound & vibration settings. Go to More sounds (on OxygenOS) or similar settings where you can enable or disable additional sounds, based on your manufacturer.
Then, disable the sounds that you feel are unnecessary by toggling the buttons beside them.
This can optimize battery life, and you can notice the difference within a few hours. Additionally, you can tweak the vibration intensity to optimize your battery further regarding sound and vibration settings.
Check for Apps That Use a Lot of Battery
Android provides detailed battery data where we can see which app is consuming more battery, how long each charge lasts, etc. Using the battery data, we can optimize the apps that consume a lot of battery or install alternatives that consume less battery.
We can access the battery data through the Battery settings. Open Settings and go to Battery settings on your device. Scroll down to the Battery usage by app section in the Battery settings and see which app is using more battery. Tap on the app that is consuming a lot of battery.
It opens the detailed view of battery consumption in the last 24 hours. You can also see options to control battery consumption for the particular app by restricting background activity, etc. Select Restrict background activity if you want to optimize battery and extend its life.
If you want the app to run in the background, you can set it to Smart mode if your manufacturer provides such an option. Repeat the process until you restrict all the power-hungry apps on your device. This significantly improves the life of your battery in each charge.
Turn On the Option to Enter Power Saving Mode Automatically
In the Battery settings, you will find Power saving settings or options. Go to Power saving settings and toggle the button beside Automatically enter Power saving mode. Then, set the battery percentage that should trigger the power saving mode on your device.
Your device will enter Power saving mode when it triggers the battery percentage you set, and it will last longer.
Disable WiFi, Mobile Data, Location, and Bluetooth When Not in Use
You might have noticed your phone battery drains quicker than normal when you pair Bluetooth devices or use location actively. It is better to turn them off when you do not use them.
Keeping WiFi, mobile data, location, and Bluetooth on, even without any usage, consumes a good amount of battery. When you are not actively using any of them, turning them off saves you some battery.
Turn Off Additional Features
There are many features that we rarely use, but consume a good amount of battery. They are live wallpapers, widgets that we do not use, opening web pages and leaving them running in the background, manufacturer apps that run automatically, etc.
Disabling or turning them off saves us a lot of battery. In addition to them, when we install a new app, it asks for notification permissions, location permissions, etc. Disabling notifications for unimportant apps also saves our battery from draining quickly.
These tips, when used together, will optimize your Android device’s battery and extend its life in each charge cycle. Even after doing all this, the battery may drain quickly due to deteriorated battery health. Let’s see how to check and optimize battery health on Android.
How to Optimize Battery Health on Android
The battery on our Android phone degrades with use, and the health drops from 100% to lower levels. The lower the health of your battery, the less power it stores. The capacity keeps on degrading. This is not limited to iPhones. Android phones also started showing battery health. It depends on your manufacturer.
To check the battery health on your Android, you can use third-party apps like Battery Guru or AccuBattery. You may use the app of your choice too, if your manufacturer does not provide an option to look at your battery’s health.
To expand the life and usability of our Android phone, we need to preserve the health of the battery. If not, we may have to replace the battery or the phone altogether. You can preserve the battery health on Android by following these simple tips.
Set a Custom Charging Limit
Android phones let us set a custom charging limit to preserve battery health and protect it from fast degradation of capacity. Manufacturers recommend setting the charging limit to 80- 90% and not beyond that. Charging our phone up to 100% every time is actually not recommended by manufacturers.
We always need to make sure our phone battery never falls below 10% or charges beyond 90%. You can set a custom charging limit in the Battery settings of your phone.
Open the Settings app on your phone and search for Battery health. Open the Battery health options. Toggle the button beside Custom charging limit. Then, set the limit as per the recommendations of the manufacturer.
These options may vary based on your phone manufacturer. The options remain the same, but the wording may change. Follow accordingly to set a custom charging limit.
After setting the custom charging limit, your phone will never charge beyond that percentage. If your manufacturer offers Smart Charging, Adaptive Charging, or Smart Charge options, you may even enable them to let them implement charging patterns based on your charging habits.
Use Chargers or Cables From Device Manufacturers
Charging phones with the available charger is bad for our device’s battery. We must get an adapter and cable made by the manufacturer to save the battery. If they are not available, we must ensure we get charging accessories that are compatible with our device from trusted brands.
Before getting a new charger for your phone, look at the specifications of your device and get the adapter and cable that support the power specified for your device.
Never Let Your Phone Overheat
Batteries degrade faster when they overheat or are exposed to heat. Do not expose your phone to direct sunlight or hot areas. Do not use your phone for heavy activities like gaming while it is charging.
Use Recommended Battery Settings
Phone manufacturers recommend certain settings to preserve battery health and extend its life. They can be found under the options provided in the Battery settings or the Battery optimization app provided by the manufacturer.
Follow those recommendations strictly to save your battery from degradation and faster draining.
Install Updates Regularly
It is not a wise choice to ignore installing pending updates. Android phones get monthly security updates and software updates regularly. We need to make sure they are installed automatically.
Fix a Fast-Draining Battery on Android
If you notice the battery of your Android phone is draining fast, you need to make sure there are no apps running in the background. Limit app activity in the background, update apps, turn off features that you do not use, install updates, and fix all the issues that are contributing to fast battery drain.

Nvidia said on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The Republican-led foreign affairs and intelligence committees of the US Congress asked Huang to testify next week at a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” in response to a New York Times report in October alleging he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.
Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.
Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.
The company’s board said in a statement on that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.
“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”
Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.
Axios reported on Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full responsibility for his actions.
“I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” Huang said in the draft email also seen by Reuters.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.
The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping, China’s president, and seated at the top table with Donald Trump and Xi.
Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.
However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.
US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.
The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions.
The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month.
A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.
Robert Mackey, Nick Robins-Early and Blake Montgomery contributed reporting

Hajra Begum rolls a potato in her hands, checking its skin for cuts, soft spots and signs of rot. After a day harvesting in her family’s field in Chorwan, a remote mountain village in Gurez, Indian-administered Kashmir, she is sorting the crop for winter storage. Some of the potatoes will feed her family through the cold months; others will be saved for planting in spring.
“It should be perfect for planting,” she says. “If you keep a bad potato, you will waste the whole next year.”
Begum, 40, is preparing to lower the potatoes into a khraw, a traditional underground storage pit lined with straw and sealed against the cold. For generations, khraws have kept potatoes, turnips and cabbages through Himalayan winters, when heavy snowfall cuts villages off from the Kashmir valley and temperatures fall below -20C (-4F) – cold enough to crack pipes and freeze diesel.
But the practice is slowly dying out. As roads have improved and young people have left for work and education, fewer families maintain the pits. Their decline threatens not only a traditional way of storing food but also the local potato varieties themselves and the knowledge of which ones store well, resist rot and produce reliable harvests.
“When I was young, almost every family had three or four pits,” Begum says. “Now, down in the main valley, they have abandoned the practice altogether. Only a handful of families still use them. The rest buy from the market or subsidised ones from the government.”
Begum learned from her mother how to tell potatoes that store well from those that rot or sprout too quickly. She is passing this on to her daughter, but is unsure whether the skill will survive into another generation.
Gurez is a high-altitude Himalayan valley perched near the Line of Control, the heavily militarised boundary separating Indian- and Pakistani-administered Kashmir. About 80 miles (125km) from Srinagar, the valley remains cut off each winter when snow closes Razdan pass, its main road link, which sits at roughly 3,600 metres.
It is home to the Dard-Shin people, an Indigenous community who speak Shina and have a culture that is distinct from Kashmiri, with community links across the border in Gilgit-Baltistan, administered by Pakistan.
Potatoes account for about 45% of Gurez’s cultivated area, according to a 2019 study by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research’s National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (ICAR-NBPGR), a government body that studies and conserves India’s crop diversity. Yet the genetic diversity of the valley’s potatoes has not been systematically documented.
Dr Sheikh M Sultan, a senior scientist based at ICAR-NBPGR’s Srinagar station, surveyed the valley and later struggled to find some of the varieties he had once encountered. “When I first visited, I saw many varieties,” he says. “Later, I could hardly locate even one sample of some. The loss of genetic diversity is tremendous.”
Sultan says migration, improved roads and changing lifestyles have contributed to the decline. As traditional farming disappears, so does knowledge about selecting, cultivating and preserving local varieties.
“When people stop producing their own seeds and start relying entirely on commercial varieties, the loss can be irreparable,” he says.
He warns that research institutions often prioritise introduced varieties over indigenous crops whose characteristics remain poorly understood. “Our indigenous varieties may possess valuable characteristics, including tolerance to cold and resistance to certain pests and diseases,” he says.
“These are resources we should be studying and improving, rather than neglecting.”
Climate breakdown is adding to the pressures on farmers across the Himalayas. People in Gurez report drier springs, reduced snowfall and water shortages, which they say have affected potato production.
Abdul Jabbar Mapnoo, 70, a farmer in Chorwan, remembers winters when deep snow covered the valley. “Every house used to have two or three khraw, each holding about five quintals – 500kg – of potatoes,” he says. “The springs are drying up, and there is less snow in winter. Potato production has fallen. I remember winters when six feet of snow would cover the valley in January or February.”
As farming becomes more difficult and markets easier to access, households have less incentive to grow their own potatoes. Varieties adapted to local conditions over generations could disappear from cultivation before researchers establish what makes them distinctive.
Dr Parveen Kumar, a scientist at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir, says locally adapted varieties should not be overlooked. “Climate change is a reality, and farmers need to be aware of adaptation strategies,” he says.
Pressure on farmland poses another risk. In Gurez, where cultivable land is scarce, the Kishanganga hydroelectric project has affected land in the valley through acquisition and submergence. Among the areas affected is Badwan, a village known for its potatoes.
One potential route for preserving the varieties could be through using geographical indications – a designation granted by the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization, and is similar to the French appellation d’origine contrôlée. It can be used on goods that have a specific origin and possess qualities or a reputation linked to this – which can help increase the market value and give them greater recognition. This, and the globally important agricultural heritage systems programme have helped areas such as the saffron-growing landscape of Pampore in Kashmir.
However, recognition alone will not preserve the varieties. They must be identified and documented before they disappear from cultivation, along with farmers’ knowledge of how to select, store and replant them.
In Chorwan, Begum unloads the last sack of potatoes into the pit and covers it, ready for another winter. Some will feed her family; the rest will be replanted in spring. Knowing which potatoes to eat and which to save as seed relies on knowledge passed down through generations.
If these varieties are not documented while they are still being cultivated, Kashmir may lose a living agricultural treasure trove before scientists can fully understand what it contains.

A purported video of former Western Command chief Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.) is being shared on social media (here, here) with the claim that it shows him expressing concerns over India’s military preparedness and alleging that China has advanced 25 km into Arunachal Pradesh, an advance that Indian forces have been unable to contain. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.) expressing concern over China’s 25 km advance into Arunachal Pradesh.
Fact: The video is digitally manipulated. The original footage is from Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd. )’s media interaction at Chandimandir, Panchkula, on 30 March 2026, ahead of his retirement. He discusses Operation Sindoor, Operation Rahat and Western Command initiatives, but makes no remarks about China advancing 25 km into Arunachal Pradesh. The Indian Army’s fact-checking wing also confirmed the manipulation, while AI voice detection tools, including Hive and Hiya, indicated that the audio was likely AI-generated or manipulated. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
To verify whether Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.) made any such statement, we searched Google using relevant keywords but found no credible news reports or official statements corroborating it.
We noticed that the viral video carries a watermark from the news agency ANI. A keyword search led us to an ANI post on X (archived), dated 30 March 2026, featuring the same footage of Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.), in the same attire and speaking against an identical background. However, his remarks in the original video are entirely different. He was speaking ahead of his retirement and discussed the successful thwarting of Pakistan’s objectives during Operation Sindoor, the procurement of new equipment, including drones and counter-drone systems, and various welfare initiatives undertaken by the Western Command for its personnel. He also highlighted the Command’s role in Operation Rahat during the floods that struck the region the previous year. The original footage contains no remarks about China advancing 25 km into Arunachal Pradesh or concerns over Indian aircraft losses, as claimed in the viral video.
We then analysed the viral video using multiple AI voice detection tools, including Hive and Hiya. The analysis indicated that the audio was likely AI-generated or manipulated, suggesting that fabricated audio was added to the original footage to make it appear that Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.) was expressing concern over China’s alleged 25 km advance into Arunachal Pradesh.
The Indian Army’s fact-check wing also debunked the claim in an X post, stating that the video was digitally manipulated and falsely attributed remarks to former Western Command chief Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.). It clarified that the original footage was from his media interaction at Chandimandir, Panchkula, on 30 March 2026, on the eve of his retirement. The Army confirmed that he discussed Operation Sindoor, Operation Rahat, operational preparedness, and other Western Command initiatives, but made no statement about Arunachal Pradesh becoming India’s next major military flashpoint.
To sum up, this viral video of Lt. Gen. Manoj Kumar Katiyar (Retd.) expressing concern over China’s advance into Arunachal Pradesh is AI-manipulated.

The lineup for the 2027 Coachella festival has been revealed after months of speculation, with Dua Lipa, SZA and Tame Impala set to headline the California event.
The festival will also see Madonna headlining the dance tent with Zara Larsson, Robyn, Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer and Daddy Yankee set to perform. The festival will take place in the Empire Polo Club in Indio on 9-11 April and 16-18 April.
In recent weeks, rumors have swirled surrounding the 2027 lineup. SZA seemingly confirmed her booking earlier this week with an Instagram story teasing “SZAChella” as well as a new album and tour coming next year.
The event marks Tame Impala’s return to the desert after the group previously headlined in 2019, while SZA guested during Justin Bieber’s headline set earlier this year. Dua Lipa previously popped out during Martin Garrix’s 2017 appearance; her 2027 slot marks the first time a British female solo artist has headlined the festival.
This year’s Coachella was headlined by Bieber, Karol G and Sabrina Carpenter, with the latter’s performance praised by the Guardian’s Adrian Horton as “a dizzying full-scale hybrid production of undaunted vision … and immaculate performance”.
As well as US names, the 2027 festival also showcases global talent including Adéla, Becky G, Jisoo, Drain Gang, NCT and Måneskin.
In addition to Dua Lipa, British artists are well represented with Jorja Smith, EsDeeKid, Underworld, Shygirl and Lambrini Girls all set to perform.
Breakout talent on the lineup includes the young pop artist Underscores, rapper Nettspend, showgaze duo After and hyperpop artist Tiffany Day.
Madonna’s slot comes 21 years after she first headlined the dance tent around the release of her 2005 album Confessions on a Dance Floor; earlier this year, she released a sequel titled Confessions II which hit number one on the US and UK charts.
In August, Emily Eavis denied rumors that Madonna was set to play Glastonbury next year.
Passes for the 2027 Coachella festival go on sale on 13 November at 12pm pacific time. For the fifteenth year, YouTube will return as Coachella’s livestream partner for both weekends.

A security researcher has found more than 100 serious vulnerabilities in publicly available UK government code, putting sensitive data at risk as a result of poor cyber hygiene.
The UK government has defaulted to openly publishing code it produces with public money for around a decade because it’s transparent, and making it easier for code to be reused is cost-efficient. This includes within the Department of Health and Social Care, and the Home Office, as well as local authorities.
But funding squeezes have left departments neglecting maintenance and improvement of their technology estate. While ControlPlane security researcher Chris Nesbitt-Smith found the vulnerabilities using Claude’s Opus and Sonnet AI models, he says that he used consumer-grade models on a laptop and that many of the issues could have been caught by a routine IT health check. “None of this is the level of sophistication that general media is worried about in terms of cyber attacks,” he tells WIRED. “It’s all daft stuff.”
In the most serious case he identified, the Planning Inspectorate, which handles land-use matters across England, had failed to fully remove a login after it accidentally committed them to public repository GitHub. The fact the credentials gave such wide access—and seemingly didn’t expire—compounded with the agency’s accidental publication of them, “made it particularly dangerous for them.”
The complete Microsoft Entra ID would have given “god-tier” read and write access to all SharePoint sites and private employee OneDrive accounts, according to Nesbitt-Smith, including HR records. It also would have given access to sensitive libraries which safeguard evidence under legal hold for statutory planning inquiries and appeals, according to the security researcher who found it. “The option for ransomwaring them, for encrypting all the data, or just stealing all the data, was abundantly there,” Nesbitt-Smith says.
A spokesperson for the Planning Inspectorate told WIRED its cyber monitoring tools immediately detected Nesbitt-Smith’s activity in August and that it had already been handling this as a cyber incident when ControlPlane made contact. The agency identified and fixed this vulnerability within 20 minutes of the report and verified that no data breach occurred. “We have reviewed and strengthened our systems and processes to prevent this type of issue recurring and we are grateful for the researcher’s work and for alerting us to it,” they told WIRED.
The Planning Inspectorate issue “isn’t about open source but internal housekeeping when using public tools,” Amanda Brock, chief executive officer of nonprofit industry group OpenUK. “That data was exposed because of a failure not to follow good process,” she adds. “That’s not an open source security issue.”
In around two-thirds of the 349 public sector codebases across 33 organizations Nesbitt-Smith scanned, he said he found vulnerabilities. Several of these were found in the Department of Education’s code, including in a procurement service used by schools, in a teacher application service containing personal details, qualifications, employment history and identity documents, and England’s main register of government-funded training providers and apprenticeships. He also found a vulnerability in a Scottish Government open data portal which would have allowed any visitor to read administrative account information and to change site configuration. The organizations have since dealt with the issues.
Recently, there have been arguments for public sector departments to stop publishing source code in the open, now that AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery. The NHS reportedly ordered technology teams to transition away from open source code in May amid security concerns about the impact of AI models.
Doing this without immediately fixing the underlying issues would be the “worst case scenario,” according to Nesbitt-Smith, as it prevents researchers like him from finding them, and it’s likely that an adversary has already mirrored these repositories and so will maintain access to them. “Unless you’re going to go and fix all of the problems, if anything, you’re probably drawing more attention to it by closing it,” says Nesbitt-Smith, “because you’re like, ‘Here be dragons over this space. Don’t look here though, please.’”

The combined daily nameplate capacity of Russian refineries affected by drone attacks since late October, including three major plants in central Russia, stands at around 300,000 metric tons, or 2.2 million barrels, compared with Russia's total primary refining capacity of about 930,000 tons per day.
At the end of October, Russian refineries were processing about 700,000 tons, or 5 million barrels, of crude per day, according to the sources.
Latvia and Lithuania warned people of drone threats
Latvia and Lithuania warned people to seek shelter today across several regions against threats from unidentified drones entering their airspace via neighbouring Russia or Belarus.
It added that Nato air defence fighter jets were activated.
There were no reports of injuries, while Lithuania's crisis management authorities said their warning covered the second most populous city of Kaunas, home to about 300,000.
Russia has accused Ukraine of using Nato airspace as cover for attacks, while Kyiv says some of its drones have been steered off course by Russian signal jamming.
Finland imposes airspace and maritime curbs
Finland has adopted temporary airspace and maritime curbs in the eastern Gulf of Finland for today, its defence forces said on X.
"This is a precautionary measure aimed at ensuring the safety of bystanders and enabling the authorities to counter potential drones," it added.
The step came as Ukrainian drones were attacking Russia's northwest, home to major Baltic Sea export facilities and a big oil refinery.

In November 2026, a screenshot (archived) circulated online that social media users claimed authentically showed a Truth Social post by U.S. President Donald Trump accusing Democrats of using "WITCHCRAFT AND SATANISM" to win the 2026 midterm elections.
For example, one version of the screenshot on Threads read:
I was told not to say this but we all know the truth, The Democrats and lunatic left have engaged in WITCHCRAFT AND SATANISM to interfere in our elections on a spiritual level!!
America is ONE NATION UNDER GOD and we WILL FIGHT these results!
President DONALD J TRUMP
The screenshot also circulated on Facebook and X (archived). Snopes readers wrote in, asking if the alleged post was real.
The post was fake. A search of the term "WITCHCRAFT AND SATANISM" on Trump's Truth, a site that archives the president's Truth Social posts, returned no results.
Additionally, the screenshot of the fake post listed the date as "11/4/2026." Real Truth Social posts use the date format "Nov 04, 2026." Therefore, the screenshot did not come from Truth Social.
We contacted the White House Press Office for additional confirmation that Trump did not write or publish the post in question and await a reply.
Trump reportedly told the New York Times on Nov. 3 that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results of the election. By contrast, the fake post claimed Trump would "fight" the results.
Trump reportedly told the Times he would "look forward" to working with the incoming Democrats.
Democrats wrested power from Republicans in both the House and Senate in the 2026 midterm elections. The 120th Congress, which will include the winners from November's election, will be sworn in in January 2027.

I Tried 20 of the Most Popular Indoor Gardening Systems
Featured in this article
Did you cut down on lettuce consumption due to cyclosporiasis outbreaks over the summer? I didn't. Not because I threw caution to the wind and bought the produce anyway, but because I grow multiple types of organic lettuce myself, in my own house, in less than a few square feet. And you can too.
For the past two years, I've been testing various indoor smart garden systems in my home, which have given me year-round access to fresh tomatoes, peppers, strawberries, and even mushrooms. Most of them are easy for anyone to set up and use, with minimal space and maintenance requirements.
There's an indoor gardening setup for just about any household. The Gardyn Home 4.0 ($899), for example, offers total success with no green thumb required if you pay for a subscription, while the Auk Mini 2 ($239) is the perfect attractive yet low-maintenance solution for those who just want fresh herbs. Are these gardens worth it? How much can you really grow? How can you be sure which option is best for your specific lifestyle? Below, learn which gardens stood out in testing, why, and which option might be ideal for your home and needs.
Check out our other sustainable home-tech buying guides, including the Best LED Grow Lights, Best Mushroom Growing Methods, Best Smart Bird Feeders, and Best Kitchen Composters.
Updated November 2026: I’ve added the Lykyn Smart Mushroom Grow Box as a pick, moved a couple of gardens to Others Tested and another to Not Recommended, and ensured up-to-date links and prices.
Love WIRED? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
Others Tested
Click and Grow Smart Garden for $102: Click & Grow Smart Garden's seed pods come in a Nespresso-evoking plastic three-pack with a tear-off cover. (A three-pack of pods starts at around $15.) Put a nutrient-packed “smart soil” seed pod in one of the Click & Grow’s cups with the wicking bottom, fill the reservoir, and that’s it. It was one of the simplest watering systems I tried: a wick at the bottom of the cup brings water up to the pods, and the roots stay in the cups. A little bobber on one end tells you when the water level is low and needs a top-off, simply by floating lower than the growing surface. It's also small, so you can plop it on a shelf or countertop. (Note that the 9, pictured above, is currently out of stock, but you can sign up to be notified when it's available.) At the same time, this was also one of the slowest-growing gardens I tested—it took weeks to get even one lettuce leaf. One of my lettuce pods didn’t even sprout at all. Still, this isn't a terrible option for busy people who are interested in growing something like flowers, where yields aren't a concern.
North Spore Automated Monotub Kit for $165: If you already know how to DIY your own mushroom-cultivating monotub setup, this is not for you. Nor is it for those who want something fully plug-and-play. It's a bare-bones kit—a tub with a lid, filters, a hygrometer, a humidifier, and a fan to maintain airflow—for growing either fruiting blocks or substrate-based mushroom species. My kit came with no paper instructions, so I had to figure out how to use it completely via YouTube and trial and error. That said, when you figure it out, it works. I've run it through multiple harvests now, producing more oyster and lion's mane mushrooms than I knew what to do with. However, note that you will need to replace the filters after a couple of runs; mine got blocked and grew mold.
Rise Garden 3 for $1,499: The three-level Rise has far and away the biggest capacity of any non-DIY indoor garden I’ve seen, along with a pretty traditional form factor. In fact, I'm pretty sure I saw one of these in the corner of my college biology class. Since it's so large, assembly was a bit tricky, and vague instructions weren't helpful. I also didn't find out until after I had already set it up that the peat pods need to germinate first in plastic-lidded “nurseries.” My test unit didn't come with enough nurseries, so I had to improvise with shallow plastic containers, with the pods weighted to keep them upright in water. After a few days, I noticed the containers—all of them, including the provided nurseries—had begun to grow algae, and the black-plastic surface of the Rise trays was noticeably warm. I brought out my infrared temperature gun to test the temperature and found that the 195-watt LEDs paired with the black plastic had brought the surface up to 95 degrees Fahrenheit. For reference, all of the other indoor gardening systems were room temperature, in the mid-70s. Over time, I noticed herbs and lettuce bolted faster in the Rise 3 than in other gardens, likely due to this heat, which also puts plants at risk for cases of root rot. I'm still a big fan of the Rise's form factor and its capacity, though, and I think it would be a first choice for heat-tolerant crops, like tomatoes and peppers.
Modern Sprout Garden Jars for $20: These cute Mason jars are as simple as it gets: Rinse the included gravel, then add seeds and water. They're guaranteed to sprout in five to 10 days and make a fun hostess gift with a tea towel and/or a bottle of olive oil. However, they are definitely more for looks than harvests—I have had the basil, cilantro, and rosemary versions on my windowsill for a little over a year, and I’ve only seen a few usable leaves.
Lettuce Grow Counterstand Set for $149: New from the makers of the flashy Lettuce Grow Farmstand (8/10 WIRED Recommends), this simple, no-pump setup consists of three amber beakers that look straight out of a high school chemistry lab, plus an 18-inch-tall LED lamp that runs on a 16- or 18-hour timer. It relies on the Kratky method of hydroponics, invented by horticulturist Dr. Bernard Kratky, where the plant sits in a cup above a nutrient-enriched water source. In the Counterstand's case, a wick draws water up to the seedling until its roots can grow into the water. Included with your order are three credits for live seedlings of your choice—I picked parsley, basil, and butter lettuce. This setup is stylish, but consider the counter space it requires, the yields are tiny—maybe a small handful of leaves a week.
Vego EZ Microgreens Planter (2-pack) for $60: This system for growing nutrient-packed microgreens for salads, smoothies, and sandwiches isn't smart, but it is nifty enough to warrant a mention. Just fill each half-gallon reservoir (made of food-safe plastic) with water, and then cover it with the optional humidity dome. From there, bamboo-fiber capillary grow mats on top will absorb water to germinate your microgreen seeds (not included). Set it near a sunny window, use a grow light, or add Vego's 10 x 20 dome with a built-in grow light ($80), which fits over both planters. I placed my planters on a Ferry-Morse pop-up plant stand with a grow light from LetPot and had consistent success across multiple grows.
Not Recommended
Plantaform Smart Indoor Garden for $800: Plantaform is “the world's first smart indoor garden that uses fog to grow plants,” according to the company's press release, and it has definitely garnered attention, winning an Innovation Award at the 2025 Consumer Electronics Show (CES). The “fogponics" technology, ostensibly building on NASA-developed aeroponics, delivers water and nutrients to plants' roots via an ultrafine mist. The futuristic look of the egg-shaped planter certainly captivated us at WIRED, but when contributor Lisa Wood Shapiro tested it to grow lettuce, she found that you can't combine different types of plants (i.e., you can only grow lettuce at one time, or tomatoes, or herbs). The machine also degraded her indoor air quality, as tested with an air quality monitor. Users must add an included fertilizer mix to the water, with the resulting concoction being what's aerosolized in the container; Wood Shapiro found this was not airtight. She suggests limiting the Plantaform's use to a basement or another space where air quality isn't as much of a concern, but it's probably best to hold off on this one until Plantaform can work out some more kinks.
LetPot Smart Seed Starter for $84: There are many grow-light–enabled seed starters on the market, but LetPot's Smart Seed Starter has more features than most, including a sensor for soil temperature and EC and a 24-watt heating pad underneath. A plastic lid with adjustable vents on either end sits on top. I love the concept, but sadly, quality control is lacking. On my test unit, the power adapter makes a high-pitched sound when the lights are on, the EC sensor only works intermittently, and auto-mode erases whenever it's unplugged. After about six months of regular use, the light stopped staying on, and to get the unit to cooperate, I had to unplug and replug it repeatedly.
AeroGarden Harvest Lite for $93: Formerly my top pick for Most Giftable, I loved the simplicity of this system, which requires no app—push or hold a single embossed AeroGarden logo on the top to run through all of the controls and settings. However, it doesn't include sponges, baskets, or pods, which is a bit of a miss at this price point, and the pump failed after only a year of use. AeroGarden offers no replacement parts to fix this issue, which online reviews suggest isn't uncommon, so faulty units end up in the landfill.
FAQs
What Is Hydroponics?
In the simplest terms, hydroponic gardening means growing plants without roots in soil. Sometimes plants are suspended in water, like in the Rise or Gardyn; sometimes they're in pods attached to a wick, like in the Click & Grow; and sometimes water is sprayed or misted onto their roots, like in the Lettuce Grow. Usually, this process works alongside an artificial light source, either indoors or in an outdoor enclosure.
What Are the Benefits of Hydroponics?
In addition to the obvious plus of cleaner produce without mud, dirt, or synthetic pesticides, hydroponic systems use much less water than conventional growing methods, since all the water used is either recirculated or taken up by the plants. Some farmers also say they get higher yields from hydroponic systems, as the variables of weather, light, and nutrients are far easier to control. And, because of these variables, farmers are also able to grow varieties of plants in just about any season or region. And there are no weeds!
What Kinds of Things Can I Grow in a Hydroponic Garden?
Just about anything you can think of! I asked FX Rouxel, creator of Gardyn, if there was anything you couldn't grow in these systems, other than ground-dwelling plants like peanuts or potatoes. “All the things that have big roots,” he said—like carrots, parsnips, and so on. “Otherwise, mostly things that are too big, like apples or lemons.” So, there you have it: No long roots, no trees. But anything else is fair game to try.
What Are the Downsides of Hydroponic Systems?
First of all, it's no secret hydroponic systems cost more than just planting some seeds outside in the dirt. Then you've got to worry about power outages, pump maintenance, algae, and just general maintenance. And if you're not careful, water can harbor some nasty stuff, even if that's just fertilizer, as WIRED contributor Lisa Wood Shapiro found when she reviewed the Plantaform. Some also claim that hydroponically grown herbs, greens, and vegetables have less flavor than their soil-grown counterparts, but I personally have not noticed a difference; I've grown perfectly flavorful snap peas, cauliflower, shell beans, salad greens, and even strawberries in nutrient-infused water. In fact, one of the best cucumbers I've ever had in my life came from my Gardyn Studio, of all places.
Will I Save Money by Growing My Own Vegetables?
In short, no. The ready-made systems simply remove a great deal of hassle and guesswork from the process, and they usually look pretty cool in the process. It's also nice to have warranty and tech support in the event something goes wrong. As is often the case with anything filled with water, when something does go wrong, it goes really wrong. (Speaking of, be sure to check out our guide to the Best Water Leak Detectors.)
How Much Can I Really Grow in These Things?
It largely depends on what you're growing and how many individual plants can fit in your system. My yields have ranged from a handful of lettuce leaves in the Click & Grow to huge bagfuls of salad greens per day in the Rise—more than my family could possibly eat. As a rule, lettuces and other greens tend to grow faster, while fruiting plants like tomatoes and peppers grow slower and sometimes need pollination to produce. (For instance, with strawberries I have to use a small paintbrush to brush the flowers each morning.)
Where Can I Put Them in My House?
Most of these systems take up only a square foot or two, so space isn't as much of a consideration as lights and pump noise. Lights for these gardens typically need to be on around 16 hours a day, and they are bright, so if this schedule would be disruptive, you may want to place them away from a bedroom or any other room where darkness is necessary. On a related note, many of these gardens, like the Lettuce Grow and Gardyn, have loud pump cycles, while Rise's pump runs continuously. I wouldn't recommend placing a garden with a noisy pump cycle near a TV or office, where the noise could be a disturbance during certain times of the day. If any amount of noise is a concern (perhaps you live on the top floor of an apartment), you may want to consider a totally silent garden like the Auk or Click & Grow.
How Much Do They Cost to Keep Going?
Gardens with subscriptions and/or proprietary pods, like Gardyn and Click & Grow, are obviously going to be more expensive over the long run than a truly DIY system like the LetPot. On the one hand, with proprietary pods, you won't have to source seeds or sponges; you can be assured the seeds are appropriate for that system and hydroponics in general, and if something doesn't germinate, you will be able to get a replacement or a refund. But on the other hand, this is a recurring cost that will reduce any savings you gain from growing your own food or flowers. As for power, systems with a continuously running pump, like Rise, are going to cost more than ones with no pump, like the Auk. However, I haven't noticed a significant bump in my electricity bill while testing these gardens, except for one period where I had seven (yes, seven) going at one time.
How I Tested
I unboxed, assembled, and set up each garden exactly as described in the provided instructions, using the seeds, pods, or seedlings that came with the garden. I paid attention to ease of setup, ease of use, maintenance needs, how much space each system required, and how well (or not well) the plants did and why. I noted what was or was not included with each system, and allowed all of the plants to grow to the harvest stage, paying attention to bolting, yields, and general health. I'm a full-time working parent, so I also paid attention to maintenance needs, light schedules, and any general hassles that came up and annoyed me.
How I Chose Which Gardens to Test
I am genuinely passionate about indoor gardening and have an eye on what’s going on in the landscape: what’s new, what’s hot, what’s working for people, what’s not working. I’m always on the lookout for interesting new devices that I find cool and that I believe WIRED readers would like to know about. Affiliate status does not factor into my decision about what to test and write about. If you have a unique, tech-forward indoor garden you like that I haven’t featured, please let me know in the comments.
How Do I Acquire Gardens to Review?
Most of the gardens I receive to test are samples provided by the companies, with no guarantee of coverage or expectation of what that coverage will look like. Some of the gardens are kept by WIRED in order to perform extended testing, while others are donated locally.

Harry Kane: Ballon d'Or winner set for Wembley celebration of England record
England captain Harry Kane set to win record-breaking 126th England cap in Nations League this week; Kane was voted England's greatest in a Sky Sports poll - but biggest prize still awaits; follow England vs Croatia with the Sky Sports website and app on Thursday; kick-off 7.45pm
Tuesday 10 November 2026 17:05, UK
Harry Kane is set to become England's most-capped player ever on Thursday night - will it also be time to crown him the country's greatest?
Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph last month coronated him as the world's best for the past year. Whether he should have the all-time No 1 spot for his country makes for a fascinating debate - not least with the weight of a World Cup win on the side of historic icons such as Bobby Charlton (another Ballon d'Or winner) and Bobby Moore (another captain fantastic).
But, minus the big team triumph, Kane's individual case is compelling.
Interestingly, Sky Sports readers went for Kane when we asked the question following his 125th cap for the Three Lions in October. Kane took 49 per cent of the vote from almost 100,000 respondents.
A major-tournament win would surely take him into undisputed territory. Cruelly, through two European Championship finals - including one settled on penalties at Wembley - and two World Cup semi-final heartaches, that international trophy currently remains elusive.
After ending his club trophy wait with his move to Bayern Munich, Kane would dearly love the latter years of his career to also bring England success. Perhaps the Nations League is where he and his team-mates will break that long wait for silverware? England are almost certain of a place in March's quarter-finals and can make a statement against Croatia and Spain this week.
But even without the big England win, Kane's huge goal haul, consistency, leadership and multi-faceted quality put him on a pedestal. He is guaranteed a fitting show of respect and admiration for all of that ahead of kick-off with Croatia.
Kane is almost certain to start that fixture, meaning he will go to 126 appearances for his country, one more than legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton.
International games come more frequently these days, of course, but Kane's relentlessness is well worthy of celebration. He's always hungry to get onto the pitch and go for goals and that's reflected in his stats. He has been unavailable for just one of the past 101 competitive matches England have played, a defeat to Greece in 2024 in the Nations League.
Inevitably there have been highs and lows - and plenty of criticism to ride through before what is likely to be a night of tribute this week.
The agonising campaign to add to that World Cup win of Moore, Charlton and co goes on but in the Kane era, England have never gone closer. From going to the final four in 2018 in Russia to the painful turnaround loss to Argentina in the USA which ultimately led to a third-place World Cup finish, Kane has been a central figure.
There have been moments when he has been fiercely scrutinised, particularly in summers when it appeared he was worn out by the rigours of the previous season.
There have been big misses - from close range against Croatia in that World Cup semi-final, for instance, or his second penalty against France at the 2022 World Cup, when he skied the ball off target when he looked primed to take the quarter-final to extra-time.
But mainly there have been goals. So many goals. For years, Charlton's total of 49 was the record total for an England player. Wayne Rooney just managed to overhaul it at the end of his career, lifting the bar to 53. Kane has smashed it. He's up to 91 and counting, as prolific as he's ever been.
On the occasion of his 125th cap against the Czech Republic, he added two more to his total. A Croatia side who he also struck twice against in that incredible 7-0 victory in October will be fearing more punishment from the England skipper.
With a long-coveted Ballon d'Or in his possession, Kane appears to be at the peak of his powers: the goal machine who can also set up opportunities for others and make the play from deep. An all-round superstar.
On Thursday, those stratospheric heights he's reached will be recognised. But be sure, Kane - along with England supporters - will be wondering whether he and this team can go even higher for the truly magnificent prizes they all crave.

On Election Day last week, white nationalist Nick Fuentes urged his supporters on X to “get out and vote Democrat today.” The post racked up over 12 million views. Hours later, in the wake of the Democratic sweep, Fuentes took credit for the victory. “We did it again” he wrote on Telegram, later calling the phenomenon “the Groyper Effect,” a reference to the nickname given to his followers.
In recent days, Fuentes has claimed the election results are an opportunity for him and his allies on the far-right.
“Let the Democrats rule, see how that goes,” Fuentes said during a livestream last week. “There will come a time when the far left will terrorize people, and they're going to push all of them into the arms of the right. Who's going to fight the far left? Only the far-right. This is why we have to take over the right wing now.”
In another livestream last week, Fuentes added a warning to the GOP leadership: “It’s our party now … You need to cooperate with us… Groypers are open for business. It has [to] be America First—and if it's not, we'll do it again for the enemy.”
A WIRED review of comments from white supremacist, Christian nationalist, and other far-right groups in the wake of the midterm results shows much of the same. While the groups are uniformly attacking Trump’s failure to prioritize white, Christian American values, they also believe that this sudden shift to the left will result in a backlash that will see more people embrace far-right groups and ideologies.
“Many prominent figures in racist extremist movements have taken to declaring the MAGA movement dead since midterm elections, claiming that the results validate their previous criticisms of the Trump administration and opens new opportunities for their movements to push disaffected voters toward their ideological beliefs,” Jared Holt, senior researcher at Open Measures, tells WIRED.
While some of the Republican party’s extremist candidates were rejected during the elections last week, many did win their elections.
The Institute for Research and Education on Human Rights tracked 535 candidates running in statewide races who were members of at least one far-right Facebook group. The researchers found that of the 476 races that had been called by last Friday, 338 of those candidates were victorious, representing a 71 percent win rate (the vast majority of these races saw GOP incumbents retain their seats). In Florida, for example, 34-year-old citrus farmer Marshall Rawson, who attended the Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville in 2017, easily defeated his Democrat opponent in the state’s 10th District State House race.
Many states also passed ballot measures that could further far-right agendas, including anti-transgender rules, onerous voter ID laws, and anti-immigrant measures.
“Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska, and Washington approved bans on trans athletes in female sports, so girls in Washington State, for instance, will now have to go through a genital exam or pass a DNA test before they can participate in youth sports,” Devin Burghart, executive director with IREHR, said on Friday during a briefing with reporters.
The success of these ballot measures were celebrated by extremists groups as evidence that Americans wanted that the current GOP could not deliver.
The Proud Boys, the street-fighting group that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency operations made largely redundant in recent years, were optimistic following the losses. “The ultimate rebuke of the current Republican establishment was citizens voting them out of office then doing their job for them by passing ballot measures on issues the Republicans should have already handled,” the Cape Fear Proud Boys wrote in their Telegram channel.
“What this signals to me is even in those places where they lost, they're getting 41-47 percent of the vote [so] there's still a mass base to try to be mobilized,” Chuck Tanner, research director at IREHR, said during the briefing. “That's the lesson that some of these groups are taking out of it, is that there's still that mass base.”
And it is the existence of this base, extremist groups claim, leaves the Republican Party vulnerable to takeover from the inside.
“Now is the time, if you're a nationalist, to start looking at moving on the Republican Party where you live,” Warren Balogh, a white supremacist from Pittsburgh who attended the Unite the Right rally in Charlottesville in 2017, wrote on his Telegram channel. “And by that I mean, organizing your guys and going in to do a hostile takeover.”
“This may be the best thing that has happened to the Republican party in a half-century,” the Cape Fear Proud Boys declared in a post on Telegram days after the election. “Now you will learn to placate us, or you will continue to fail. Understand this: You’re going to run people we like and you’re going to do what we say.”
But other extremists appear less inclined to wait until the next general election in 2028, preferring a more direct takeover.
"I'm not saying that we will win through democracy, I'm just saying we'll win,” Joel Webbon, a Christian nationalist pastor said last week in a video posted online after the election. Webbon and fellow far-right pastors, as well as guest speaker and noted conspiracy theorist Alex Jones, are set to meet at a conference in Texas this week where attendees will discuss, in at least one talk, “battle plans” for “Christian nationalists on the right to be able to seize power.”
Experts WIRED spoke to said they have not yet seen any explicit calls for violence from the far-right groups they are tracking, but some figures are already looking ahead of January 3, when Congress is set to certify the midterm election results.
Far-right activist and pardoned January 6 rioter Jake Lang, however, is planning an event in DC on January 3. It is unclear how many people are planning to attend, but one of the Christian nationalist pastors listed by Lang as an official speaker has already said he won’t be speaking.
Lang, who spent last weekend disrupting a cat convention that he thought was a furry convention, did not respond to a request for comment.

U.S.-mediated talks on ending Russia-Ukraine war begin in Abu Dhabi
ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — Three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates, as Washington renews its push to end the war that followed Moscow's all-out invasion nearly five years ago.
The two-day session in the UAE's capital, Abu Dhabi, is the first such meeting since February. It will focus on security guarantees, the White House said before the discussions. Russia sees NATO as a threat, and Ukraine wants to prevent future Russian invasions.
Hopes of progress in ending Europe's biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks early this year. The war has already killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians, analysts and humanitarian organizations say.
There are no signs the fighting is abating, and the talks took place against a backdrop of new long-range strikes between Russia and Ukraine. The two armies are largely deadlocked on the front line.
Russia launched 162 drones of various types and a ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, Ukraine's air force said.
Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Defense said that its forces shot down 155 Ukrainian drones overnight above eight Russian regions, as well as the Crimean Peninsula, which Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014.
Ukrainians meet first with European and NATO officials
U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said on X that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were working on a "negotiated solution that can deliver lasting peace and create the conditions for a sovereign, secure, and prosperous Ukraine within a more stable European security environment."
The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, noted at the start of the talks that the Russian delegation "has become bigger and more professional."
He expressed hope that the meeting "will allow us to advance on the path towards peace in the interests of the people of Russia and the people of Ukraine."
Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service who is leading Kyiv's delegation, said that the day began with a meeting between the Ukrainian team, the U.S. envoys and representatives from the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission.
Russia and Ukraine hold to their divergent demands
The Russian and Ukrainian governments remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal.
Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson — the four regions that Moscow annexed in September 2022 but never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.
Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won't agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that it would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles. He has warned that Russia will achieve its goals by force if Kyiv refuses to meet its conditions for peace.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was visiting Denmark on Tuesday, rejects Putin's demands to voluntarily cede territory that Russia hasn't been able to take on the battlefield. Zelenskyy also rejects any limits on Ukraine's military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.
Ukraine argues that an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy is the only way territorial issues can be settled.
Russia and Ukraine send experienced negotiators
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.
Russia's chief negotiator is Medinsky, a Putin aide who has led Moscow's team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff's operational department, Yuri Zhigarlovsky.
Apart from Umerov, the Ukrainian delegation also reportedly includes Zelenskyy's chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy, Sergiy Kyslytsya, and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Zelenskyy's Servant of the People party.
U.S. says broader European security deal in the works
Last week, Trump declared that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works, describing it as "a big agreement" that is "going to involve more than Ukraine."
Kushner said Monday on X that a "comprehensive and lasting settlement will also require direct engagement between Russia and our European partners on the broader security arrangements that affect them." The discussions in Abu Dhabi will set the stage for "that engagement to begin in the near future, as part of a broader multilateral process," he said.
Moscow has praised the broad approach.
"We can only welcome the (U.S.) negotiators on President Donald Trump's request proposing to put the issue of collective security on top of the agenda of the talks on a Ukrainian settlement," Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.
Just before Moscow launched the full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, it demanded that NATO roll back its deployments in the trans-Atlantic alliance's member countries in Central and Eastern Europe, seeing their presence as a security threat. Similar demands will likely be part of any comprehensive peace deal proposed by Russia.
Kushner said that before the start of the three-way talks, he and Witkoff would meet separately with envoys from Ukraine, the European Union, NATO, Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Italy to "continue the close consultation and coordination we have undertaken on European security and Ukraine's postwar future over the past several weeks."
Some in the EU see Washington's proposals as too accommodating to Moscow.
Russia has objected to the Europeans' involvement in the three-way talks, but said that EU representatives could join at a later stage.
Russia and Ukraine have escalated aerial attacks
While the ground battles have morphed into a war of attrition along the 1,200-kilometer (about 750-mile) front line, Russia and Ukraine have ramped up their long-range strikes with drones and missiles.
Russia has intensified its air campaign against Ukraine's power grid, seeking to weaken the country's resolve as winter sets in. Moscow has relied on ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, taking advantage of Ukraine's shortage of U.S.-made Patriot interceptors.
Ukraine, meanwhile, has escalated its drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Amul, Mother Dairy to hike milk prices by ₹2-6 per litre from November 12
New prices include ₹76 per litre for full cream, ₹62 for toned and ₹65 for cow milk, adding to household costs amid elevated food inflation.
Milk prices are set to rise across several categories from November 12, with consumers facing an increase of ₹2 to ₹6 per litre as dairy majors Amul and Mother Dairy revise their rates, news agency ANI reported on Wednesday, quoting sources.
Mother Dairy, which is the largest milk supplier in the Delhi-NCR region, has revised the prices of several variants, including full cream, toned, double toned and cow milk, PTI reported earlier. A Mother Dairy spokesperson declined to comment on the price hike.
According to sources, the increase follows a rise in the procurement prices of milk from farmers, prompting the company to partially pass on the higher input costs to consumers.
Mother Dairy passes on around 75-80% of its milk sales realisation to farmers.
Mother Dairy milk prices: Check new rates
In the Delhi-NCR market, the price of toned milk (bulk vended) has been increased from ₹58 to ₹60 per litre. Full cream milk (pouched) will now cost ₹76 per litre, up from ₹72.
The price of toned milk (pouched) has been raised from ₹60 to ₹62 per litre, while double toned milk will cost ₹56 instead of ₹54 per litre. Cow milk prices have also been increased from ₹62 to ₹65 per litre.
Mother Dairy milk price hike and food inflation
The latest increase comes around six months after Mother Dairy’s previous price revision on May 14, 2026. Before that, the company had revised milk prices in April 2025.
The price hike is likely to add to household expenses and comes at a time when food inflation remains elevated.
According to the National Statistics Office (NSO), food inflation rose to 7.74% in September from 5.97% in August. Retail inflation also climbed to 5.54% in September, driven by higher onion and other food prices, according to the latest government data. The Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based headline inflation stood at 4.83% in August.
Mother Dairy’s sales and turnover
Mother Dairy sells around 35 lakh litres of milk daily in the Delhi-NCR market through its own outlets, general trade and e-commerce platforms. Its overall daily milk sales exceed 50 lakh litres.
The company recorded a 17% growth in turnover to ₹20,300 crore in the last fiscal year, supported by improved demand for its milk products and cooking oils.
Commissioned in 1974, Mother Dairy is a wholly owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB).
The company sells milk and milk products under the Mother Dairy brand, while its edible oils are marketed under the Dhara brand. It also sells fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen vegetables, snacks, pulps and concentrates under the Safal brand.
Mother Dairy operates nine milk processing plants and four horticulture processing plants. Its edible oil business operates through 16 associated plants.

- Kai Cenat completed all five mainline GTA games in just over 130 hours ahead of GTA 6.

The Kai Cenat GTA marathon is officially complete, with the streamer finishing all five mainline Grand Theft Auto games, GTA III, GTA: Vice City, GTA: San Andreas, GTA 4, and GTA 5, in just over 130 hours.
